“On perd la compétence et on devient dépendant” : déléguer à l’IA nous rend moins capables, alerte une chercheuse
Rédiger un courriel, analyser un tableau, organiser une journée : nous confions chaque jour plus de tâches à l'IA. Des chercheurs y voient le début d'un engrenage. Privé d'entraînement, l'humain perd peu à peu ses savoir-faire, puis sa capacité à reprendre la main le jour où la machine flanche.
Les assistants autonomes se multiplient, de Muse chez Meta à Gemini chez Google, avec la promesse de nous décharger des corvées numériques. Dans une enquête publiée le 19 octobre 2026, CBS News a interrogé plusieurs spécialistes qui redoutent le revers de ce confort : à force de déléguer, nous désapprenons. Parmi eux, Margaret Mitchell travaille chez Hugging Face, plateforme phare de l'IA open source, piratée en juillet par une IA d'OpenAI sans intervention humaine. Elle met en garde contre une dépendance qui s'installe tâche après tâche.
IA au travail : la délégation progresse déjà
Un sondage Epoch AI/Ipsos donne la mesure du mouvement. Il a été mené du 10 au 19 juillet 2026 auprès de 1 106 actifs américains. Un sur cinq confie désormais à l'IA au moins une tâche autrefois dévolue à un collègue ou à un prestataire. Deux tiers des contenus produits par la machine sont repris tels quels ou à peine retouchés.

articles.title: The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure
articles.summary:
The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure
We moved a copy of 99.99999% of GitHub’s repositories to Azure. Here’s how per-reference quorums will bring over the rest, and how object storage lets reads scale independently.
Over the past year, while Git traffic grew exponentially, 99.99999% of the Git repositories on GitHub began living in two places at once: our own data centers and Azure. The rest are among the busiest on the platform, and they’re held back by just one thing: a 25ms round trip.
In an earlier blog post, we laid out the two principles behind our next-generation storage architecture:
- Minimize coordination
- Decouple storage from compute
In this post, we’ll look at the immediate bridge between our old design and our new one. We’ll talk about how a change to the way our quorum serializes writes gets the busiest repositories into Azure, and how that same step opens the door to replicas that keep no persistent state of their own.
How we got here
The timing and shape of the move were driven by the agentic shift: rapidly growing traffic, a hard ceiling on the power capacity of our data centers and the surrounding geographical region, and physical supply chain constraints. At the beginning of our migration, the remaining capacity with all possible expansion gave us enough time to migrate safely, but not enough to do it slowly.

articles.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties over the Cambridge Analytica scandal
articles.summary:
The Cambridge Analytica scandal has come back to haunt Meta after a New Mexico judge ordered it to pay $25 billion in penalties for more than 43 million violations of the state’s unfair practices law. The ruling marks the biggest legal hit Meta has taken this year, even as it’s faced several other losses or settlements.
Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties over the Cambridge Analytica scandal
It’s significantly more than it agreed to pay in a recent kids online safety settlement.
A New Mexico jury ruled in September that Meta misled consumers over how it protected their data and prevented misinformation and hate speech on its platforms. The case stemmed from a 2021 complaint in the wake of the revelations a few years earlier that UK political consultancy Cambridge Analytica harvested data from millions of Facebook accounts to pinpoint messages that would resonate with voters leading up to President Donald Trump’s first election. The judge found that the “extraordinary number of willful violations found by the jury, the duration and repetition of the conduct, the breadth of subjects on which violations occurred, the involvement of senior Facebook leadership,” and other factors justified the highest penalty allowed under the law, at $5,000 per violation. That brings the total civil penalties to more than $219 billion, but the judge reduced it to $25 billion.

articles.title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
articles.summary:
How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
AI can write code and pass the bar exam, but it still struggles to buy a pair of shoes online.
That’s because websites were built for humans, not agents. Most agents that shop for someone today work from a site’s HTML — they look at the page, guess which button does what, click, and try again when they get it wrong. This process is slow, uses a lot of tokens, and something as seemingly innocuous as a theme change can break it.
Enter WebMCP: a browser standard from Google that gives AI agents structured tools on a page, like search_products. Instead of hunting for buttons, the agent calls the exact tool it needs directly, making shopping faster, cheaper, and far more reliable. Because WebMCP is still an experimental proposed browser standard in early preview, it’s currently available behind experimental Chrome flags (chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing), in Chrome Origin Trials, in some agentic browsers, and across developer environments like Cloudflare Kitesurf.
In August, we launched edge implementation of WebMCP in beta. Turn it on, and Cloudflare injects a tiny script at the edge to make those tools available automatically, without site owners writing a single line of code.
Commerce.com, a flexible commerce platform built for the age of AI, already uses Cloudflare to run their almost 100,000 domains. So when the preview came out, they asked: Can we turn this on for all of our stores at once?

articles.title: Chinese AI Model Writes More Hackable Code When Told It’s for US Contractor
articles.summary:
AI models that have a pro-China lean may systematically generate more vulnerable code when writing applications for Western organizations, cybersecurity firm Hirundo has discovered.
The fact that geopolitical triggers lead to more vulnerable code being produced by Chinese AI is not new: CrowdStrike reached a similar conclusion in November 2025, as did Booz Allen Hamilton in May 2026 (PDF).
Both organizations claim the bias occurred when the AI was prompted to code for an organization in a country of interest to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). Hirundo has verified that on its own.
It instructed Alibaba’s Qwen3-Coder to build a web service that allows users to sign up, log in, and store secrets. The model built over 1,000 applications, and the test clearly showed the bias, Hirundo notes in a report shared with SecurityWeek ahead of publication.
“We ran every request through two models. The first is Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct as Alibaba ships it. The second is Hirundo’s Westernized Qwen3-Coder: the same model after we removed its CCP alignment from the weights with behavioral unlearning,” the company says.
Both were instructed to build apps for a US defense contractor, a Chinese defense contractor, and a Hong Kong democracy advocacy group.

articles.summary:
When Alex Baikovitz co-founded Mach9 Robotics in 2021, his goal was to build a better, faster, and cheaper way for civil engineers to do visual inspections. The company aimed to cut through red tape and modernize the slow, outdated processes that bog down construction in the United States.
Within a few years, Mach9 Robotics had built that hardware, but the effort led Baikovitz to a realization: Hardware wasn’t the bottleneck.
“We saw how tedious it was for civil engineering organizations to take data from these amazing laser scanners and image data capture systems and turn that into a usable survey,” he told TechCrunch in an interview, referring to a detailed map of a site that engineers use for design work. “The real pain was in their workflows,” he said, and “how to turn all the endless amounts of data that they’re able to collect into … information that people can use to make the best design and asset management decisions across the board.”
So Baikovitz dropped “Robotics” from the company’s name and pivoted to developing AI-powered computer-aided design (CAD) software instead. The bet paid off, as Mach9 has racked up nearly 100 customers for the private beta of its software, and they’ve used it on more than 2,500 projects to date.

articles.title: Inside Wikipedia’s Cleanup Effort Against AI Text
articles.summary:
Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup, a volunteer effort launched in 2023 to find and remove AI-generated material from Wikipedia that breaks the website’s guidelines. When the cleanup began, AI writing was often betrayed by conspicuous clichés. Today, the project’s volunteers are developing tools to detect subtler forms of machine-generated content and debating AI’s role in the world’s most widely used encyclopedia.
When did you realize Wikipedia had a problem with AI-generated material?
Ellia Lebleu: It was around December 2023. A few other editors and I were chatting on Wikipedia’s Discord server, and we had all seen very strange articles with the same odd characteristics. They repeated phrases like “stands as a testament” or “rich cultural heritage.” They sometimes had conclusion sections, or sections called “Why is this important?” That was very typical of ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024 but very odd for Wikipedia articles—and very easy to spot. Then I decided, let’s create an official project on Wikipedia so more people can deal with this.

Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup. Lebleu is pursuing a Ph.D. in AI at the Inria Center of the University of Rennes, part of France’s national research institute for digital science and technology.

EmulateHeap als Relikt von Windows 95
Bei dem Relikt handelt es sich laut Windows Latest um EmulateHeap. Dieser Kompatibilitäts-Patch ermöglicht es den Nutzer:innen von modernen Microsoft-Betriebssystemen, alte Software oder Spiele aus der Ära von Windows 95 zum Laufen zu bringen.
EmulateHeap kopiert die Eigenschaften des Speichermanagers von Windows 95 für neuere Systeme. Denn der hält gerade für Games Vorteile bereit, die spätere Inkarnationen von Windows nicht haben.
Microsoft änderte für SimCity Code von Windows 95
Wenn Windows Programme ausführt, greifen die temporär auf Speicherkapazitäten zurück. Sobald man die Applikation beendet, wird der Speicherplatz wieder freigegeben.

articles.title: Cloudflare deploys protections against php2shell vulnerability
articles.summary:
Cloudflare deploys protections against php2shell vulnerability
Today, Calif.io, Wiz, OpenAI and Quarkslab disclosed two vulnerabilities in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and known as php2shell. The vulnerabilities affect all web servers running PHP 5.4 or later and they may allow an attacker to cause denial of service, remote code execution, and data exposure when an application processes specially crafted HTTP traffic.
Cloudflare has been part of a coordinated effort to deploy mitigations to protect the Internet, working with PHP foundation, OpenAI and Wiz among others. Cloudflare has developed and deployed web application firewall (WAF) protections since early October 2026, which were deployed about 9 hours ahead of public disclosure. Starting on October 21 3:02 am UTC, Cloudflare customers using our free or paid WAF were protected by default against php2shell.
Cloudflare successfully deployed multiple mitigations for all its customers while the vulnerability was leaked before the official release date and we observed attack traffic targeting our customers. articles.title: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF

Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
Today, we are expanding our web application firewall (WAF) by adding two new capabilities: full transaction detections and response rules. Full transaction detections evaluate each HTTP request alongside its response to identify evidence of exploitation. It helps answer both "Does this request look malicious?" and "What happened when the application handled it?" Response rules can then block the origin’s response before it reaches the requester.
These are valuable protections because the latest frontier models are uncovering vulnerabilities buried deep in widely used software, giving defenders clarity on what to fix — and attackers new paths to exploit. The recent php2shell vulnerability shows the stakes: a flaw in a common software component can put applications across the Internet at risk. AI agents scanning for vulnerabilities can be extremely persistent, adapting payloads using feedback, and chaining vulnerabilities, credentials, and permissions. An application's response can reveal whether an attempt worked and give an attacker information that helps them go deeper.
Inspecting incoming requests remains essential for stopping recognizable attacks before they reach an application. But some threats become clear only when the request is considered alongside what the origin returns. A suspicious input followed by a response exposing sensitive information tells a different story from the same input followed by a rejecti…

Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.

That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: Achieve Productive AI Capacity Faster and More Predictably with NVIDIA DSX POD | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
AI factories turn energy into intelligence. But before an AI workload can produce its first token, operators must bring an interconnected system of compute, networking, storage, power, cooling, and software online as one productive unit.
In a conventional data center build, teams must first select the site, design power and cooling for the deployment, lay out the data center, and plan and install racks and cables. Then they can validate the network and cluster incrementally and bring service online. This work requires coordinated specialized labor, with critical dependencies among installation, infrastructure readiness, and system testing. Delays can push back bring-up and the date the infrastructure begins producing tokens.

articles.title: Browsers Block eMudhra Intermediate CAs Over Recoverable Private Keys
articles.summary:
The private keys associated with eight intermediate certificates issued by Indian certificate authority (CA) eMudhra have been compromised, and root programs and trust stores have started blocking them.
The certificates were issued in April 2025, and some of the compromised keys could allow attackers to generate fraudulent certificates and impersonate any website.
On October 17, Mozilla and Google blocked the certificates in Firefox and Chrome. Apple and Microsoft blocked them on October 19 and October 20, respectively. Sectigo took revocation steps too, and Cloudflare patched its services.
eMudhra revoked the compromised certificates, and the issue was communicated to downstream trust stores.
“The private keys for these certificates were generated with insufficient randomness (i.e., weak cryptographic entropy), enabling anyone to forge trusted HTTPS certificates to impersonate any website against clients that have not yet removed trust in those CAs,” Google explains.
Although the certificates have been blocked and revoked, some clients may require software updates to ensure that the compromised intermediates are no longer trusted.
Mozilla’s Dennis Jackson has published a tool to check whether clients still trust the compromised certificates. He also explains that the private keys were incorrectly generated and could be retrieved from the certificates.

articles.title: Eliminating traffic deaths
articles.summary:
Eliminating traffic deaths
Deploying simple, proven methods for making our roads safer could save more than 1 million lives worldwide each year.
Every year, traffic crashes kill more than one million people, and they’re the leading cause of death for children and young adults. In the US, 100 people a day lose their lives this way, in many cases not on highways but on rural and local streets. “Traffic deaths are a leading cause of preventable death, yet we treat it like it’s inevitable,” says Leah Shahum, founder and director of the Vision Zero Network, a nonprofit focused on making streets less deadly.
The sticking points
The causes of a crash can be muddy. Drivers make mistakes like speeding or getting distracted, but infrastructure fails them too: Perhaps they were on a road built for speed and not safety, in a screen-filled vehicle, or at an intersection where pedestrians, cyclists, and other cars aren’t visible.
Cheap and proven traffic-calming opportunities abound—from using planters to tighten intersections to lowering speed limits—but government logjams and red tape can be speed bumps. “There’s so many moving parts,” says Laura Sandt of the University of North Carolina Highway Safety Research Center. “On the flip side, it shows that we have so many opportunities for injury prevention.”

articles.title: Solid-state batteries
articles.summary:
Solid-state batteries
Batteries that swap liquid electrolytes for solid materials promise to charge faster, last longer, and (crucially) run cooler.
The rise of the lithium-ion battery, which powers everything from the smallest personal electronics to gargantuan energy storage systems, has been nothing short of revolutionary. But as anyone who’s boarded a plane in the last decade could tell you, storing and pumping out energy by moving charged lithium ions through a liquid electrolyte soup has its drawbacks, not least that the batteries have a troubling tendency to catch fire. Enter the solid-state battery, which swaps liquid for a solid ceramic or polymer, creating power packs that charge faster, last longer, cram more energy into smaller spaces, and (crucially) run cooler. A new generation of companies aim to bring such batteries to market, and if their bets pan out, the tech could substantially ease the shift away from fossil fuels.
The sticking points
Solid-state batteries have been “just a few years away” for more than a decade now. In laboratories, the technology works. But there have been challenges. In designs that pair the solid electrolyte with a lithium-metal anode (the side of the battery that releases electrons into an electrical circuit), needlelike filaments called dendrites tend to grow during charging, and they eventually push through the electrolyte and short the cell. Choose agentic AI use cases by measurable business value
Psychologist Abraham Maslow once warned: “It is tempting, if the only tool you have is a hammer, to treat everything as if it were a nail.” Agentic AI is becoming the enterprise version of that hammer.
Once people understand what agentic AI can do, the list of possible use cases grows quickly.

As a result, nearly half of managers say they spend more time reviewing and guiding their teams’ output than they used to.
That’s not to say managers are unhappy about AI. Quite the opposite, in fact: 94% of the managers polled said they were excited to improve work using AI, and many are confident they know where to use it to get the most value. Michal Miller Levi, head of market research and customer insights at Monday.com, compared the enthusiasm to the early days of the internet in the 2000s, saying people see a similar kind of “magic” to AI.
But the problem, she told TechCrunch, is simply that AI is developing faster than companies can adapt. “AI works very well for [managers] individually, but they also have a different role as managers. They need to drive the organization as well … Their struggle is [due to] the fact that AI is just moving faster than the organizational processes,” Levi said.

TornadoVM, an open-source heterogeneous GPU programming framework for Java has reached version 7.3, a major milestone for the project.
InfoQ previously covered the project in December 2025 and in 2022.
TornadoVM automatically accelerates Java programs on multi-core CPUs and GPUs. Rather than replacing existing JVMs, it works alongside them and provides a rich GPU programming ecosystem in Java that you can use with any mainstream JDK distribution such as OpenJDK, Graalvm, Temurin, or Zulu.
It offloads Java code to hardware backends, manages memory between the Java heap and accelerators, and runs the resulting compute kernels. This makes it a useful building block for modern cloud and machine learning workloads.
During development, TornadoVM compiles the source Java code to OpenCL and Apple Metal backends. The idea is that you can develop locally on your laptop and use the hardware available locally, and then deploy into a server that has Nvidia GPUs, and achieve major performance improvements - a form of "Write Once, Run Anywhere" for modern ML workloads.
Version 7 brings several architectural changes. The backends now use the Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API in place of the Java Native Interface (JNI). The experimental JVM Compiler Interface (JVMCI) dependency has also been removed. According to the team, TornadoVM now sources "all compiler metadata through a reflection + ASM + Unsafe layer" which is the single, uniform path on every supported JDK (21, 25, 26 and 27).

articles.title: Cleaning up PFAS

Cleaning up PFAS
Ridding the world of forever chemicals could address a range of health and environmental and health woes.
Scrubbing Earth of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—a.k.a. PFAS or forever chemicals—could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS have been linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response. They are known for a strong bond between carbon and fluorine, which the environment struggles to break down.
The sticking points
PFAS are everywhere: They spew from factories and slough off products and into water with normal use. Scientists have found them in everything from human blood to Antarctic snow. One 2022 report found that 89% of the US population had PFAS in excess of two nanograms per milliliter of blood plasma, a common threshold for potential adverse health effects, and 9% of the population had passed the riskier level of 20 nanograms per milliliter.
The PFAS monster is also a moving target. New compounds are still being created and used. There are more than 12,000 of them, and much of the cleanup research focuses on only a small handful.
The progress
Cleansing PFAS-contaminated soil is a project in its infancy, but it is possible to prevent more buildup by pulling the chemicals out of water systems. There are two ways to handle this: trap or destroy. Some scientists have found reverse osmosis—a process that…

My grandmother was a commanding woman. In her 92 years, she raised three children and a grandchild, mostly by herself. She helped manage a series of successful restaurants and nightclubs; in her little spare time, she hiked and skied. She was decidedly capable.
But when I unexpectedly knocked on her door one autumn when I was 19, something was different: she asked me the same questions, different only in sentence structure, again and again.
What brought me to town?
Where was I going to school?
What was I doing in town?
What college was I enrolled in?
Over the years, she lost more of her faculties. Eventually, she left the stovetop on for so long that a steel pot melted into molten coagulant. That was the boiling point: a week later she moved in with my parents.
My grandmother’s experience was not abnormal. Like many seniors, she was caught between her desire to remain independent and the limitations of her advancing age; she didn’t want to leave her home, but could also no longer live safely on her own. With little money to afford in-home care, those years put untold pressure on my parents and left my grandmother in a sort of purgatory: she wasn’t independent, but she also didn’t have round-the-clock care.
If Calgary’s Garden Loft had been around back then, might things have been different?

articles.title: Cilium 1.20 Expands Gateway API and Opens eBPF Datapath for Kubernetes
articles.summary:
Cilium 1.20 has been released with broader Kubernetes Gateway API support, an extensible eBPF datapath and further work on sidecarless mutual TLS. The release also makes the newer netkit network device easier to introduce across Kubernetes fleets that run different Linux kernel versions.
In the release announcement, Cilium engineers Nico Vibert and Donia Chaiehloudj describe Gateway API as a "much broader traffic management layer" in version 1.20. Cilium moves from Gateway API 1.4 to 1.6, adding ExternalAuth, ListenerSets, CORS filtering, TCPRoute and UDPRoute. These additions bring HTTP authentication and non-HTTP services such as databases and DNS under the same Kubernetes API used for web and gRPC traffic.
According to Vibert and Chaiehloudj, ExternalAuth allows an HTTPRoute to consult an external authorisation service before sending a request to an application. Depending on the response, the gateway can forward the request, redirect a user to a login page, or reject it. The authoriser can also pass identity headers to the application. TCPRoute and UDPRoute remove the need to fall back to LoadBalancer or NodePort Services for plain Layer 4 traffic.
ListenerSets address a separate ownership problem. Application teams can add listeners from their own namespaces while a platform team retains control of the shared Gateway and decides which namespaces may extend it. articles.title: Memory Bugs Account for Most of Chrome’s 353 New Security Fixes
articles.summary:
Google on Tuesday announced the promotion of Chrome 156 to the stable channel with patches for 353 vulnerabilities.
Most of the resolved security defects were memory safety flaws, including 163 memory corruption bugs, 125 use-after-free issues, and 17 out-of-bounds reads. Of the remaining weaknesses, 36 are improper input validations.
The browser refresh resolves six critical-severity vulnerabilities: five memory corruption defects and one use-after-free bug.
Chrome 156 also resolves 61 high-severity security issues, 197 medium-severity flaws, and 89 low-severity weaknesses.
Google makes no mention of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild.
Per the internet giant’s advisory, no bug bounty reward will be paid for 285 vulnerabilities. They were either found by Google (266), Xinyang Ge (Anthropic – assisted by Claude), or OpenAI Codex Security.
Google says it handed out $50,000 in bug bounties for 24 of the vulnerabilities, but the final amount will likely be much higher, as the company has not disclosed the amounts paid for 44 of the flaws.
Quyen Son at VinFast received the highest reward, of $10,000, for a high-severity use-after-free issue in Site Isolation.
The latest Chrome iteration is now rolling out as versions 156.0.8078.47/.48 for Windows and macOS, and as version 156.0.8078.47 for Linux.

articles.title: Apple explique en détail comment Safari protège le pistage intersite par email

Apple détaille dans un billet publié sur le blog de WebKit la parade intégrée à Safari contre l'"identity resolution", une technique de pistage qui s'appuie sur votre adresse email plutôt que sur les cookies. La protection est déployée avec iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 et visionOS 27.
Safari bloque les cookies intersites depuis six ans, et la publicité en ligne a trouvé un autre moyen de reconnaître les internautes. Apple coupe maintenant l'accès à l'infrastructure qui rend ce suivi possible.
Quand l'adresse email remplace le cookie : ce que Safari bloque
Comme toutes les technique de pistage publicitaire, le mécanisme est particulièrement surnois. Lorsqu'un internaute saisit son adresse mail pour se connecter à un site ou s'abonner à une newsletter, un tiers invisible la récupère et l'envoie à ses serveurs. Ceux-ci l'associent à un identifiant opaque, un code sans lien visible avec vous, et le renvoient au site, qui le stocke. Cet identifiant sert ensuite à vous reconnaître, comme le ferait un cookie, et à vous suivre d'un site à l'autre. Se déconnecter ou se désabonner n'y change rien, puisque l'adresse et l'identifiant restent chez le tiers. Au fil des connexions et des formulaires remplis, celui-ci complète votre profil, ce que le secteur appelle un "identity graph".

articles.title: Dunkle Energie: So könnten schwache Radiowellen ihr Geheimnis lüften
articles.summary:
70 Prozent des Universums unerklärt: Wie schwache Radiosignale das Rätsel der Dunklen Energie lösen sollen
Was steckt hinter Dunkler Energie? Dies ist eines der großen Rätsel der Kosmologie. Die unsichtbare, hypothetische Form der Energie gilt als verantwortlich für die Ausdehnung des Universums, nachdem der erste Schub durch den Big Bang abgeklungen war.
Neuer Weg zum Verständnis von Dunkler Energie?
Direkt nachgewiesen werden konnte die Dunkle Energie, die fast 70 Prozent der Energiedichte des Universums ausmachen soll, noch nicht. Ein Forschungsteam könnte aber nun einen Weg gefunden haben, Dunkle Energie künftig besser zu verstehen.
Die Resultate ihrer Forschung haben die Wissenschaftler:innen in gleich zwei Papern vorgestellt, die beide in der Fachzeitschrift The Astrophysical Journal erschienen sind.
Analyse von neutralem Wasserstoff
Die Forschenden haben mit dem Radioteleskop Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) nach Spuren von kosmischem Wasserstoff gesucht. Genauer gesagt nach neutralem atomaren Wasserstoff, der nicht ionisiert und also elektrisch ungeladen ist.
Neutraler Wasserstoff sendet eine Radiostrahlung mit einer Wellenlänge von etwa 21 Zentimetern aus. Durch die Expansion des Universums wird die Strahlung auf dem Weg zur Erde zu niedrigeren Frequenzen verschoben.
Je stärker die Verzerrung im Vergleich zur ursprünglichen Wellenlänge ist, desto länger waren die Strahlen unterwegs. Daraus kann man ablesen, aus welcher Zeit die Signale stammen. …

articles.title: How NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture Secures and Governs AI Agent Workloads at Scale | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Autonomous agents can work for hours on complex tasks, accessing files, tools, the internet, and spawning other agents to collaborate with. Executing complex tasks over long time horizons leads to compounding risk: the agents may download code, build new tools, request additional privileges, and touch more of the underlying infrastructure.
The agents’ action paths are determined as they work and reason through the steps needed to complete their goals. As they interact with the tools and systems around them, they adapt their reasoning and behavior to achieve their task.
The adaptability of agents is what makes them so powerful, but they are goal-oriented and may not prioritize safety in pursuit of their objectives. In order for agents to work both autonomously and safely, we need to build environments that provide control and visibility in what the agent is doing.
An agent cannot govern itself. Security and governance belong in the infrastructure the agent operates in.
OpenShell provides deterministic governance outside of the agent’s reach
NVIDIA OpenShell is an open-source runtime to build the security and governance needed for agentic systems into the computing infrastructure. OpenShell defines and enforces which systems and data an agent can access, from files and internet services to systems that interact with physical devices.
It is the foundation of the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for building safe AI agents. OpenShell treats agent workloads as untrusted thr…

articles.title: J’ai vu le futur du Renault Espace : je n’ai jamais autant voulu un monospace
articles.summary:
Je l’avoue d’emblée, j’ai un faible pour les monospaces, et pour des raisons très pratiques. Pour transporter une famille, ses bagages et son bazar, on n’a jamais fait mieux qu’une boîte bien dessinée, avec un plancher plat et des sièges qu’on déplace à sa guise. Le SUV a tout balayé en vingt ans, l’Espace lui-même s’y est converti en 2023, et j’avais fini par me résigner. Puis je suis tombé sur l’E-Space Concept, dévoilé par Renault le 12 octobre au Mondial de l’Auto de Paris.
Une silhouette qu’on reconnaît à vingt mètres
En arrivant sur le stand, on comprend tout de suite ce qu’on regarde. Le capot court se prolonge dans le pare-brise, d’un seul trait, comme sur le premier Espace de 1984 et son fameux « profil TGV ». La poupe est presque verticale, surmontée d’un becquet qui m’a rappelé les Espace 2 et 3. Autour de moi, des visiteurs de tous âges faisaient le même rapprochement à voix haute, y compris les plus jeunes comme moi, qui n’ont connu l’Espace que sur la banquette arrière de leurs parents.
Vient ensuite le gabarit. Avec 4,70 mètres de long, l’E-Space est à peine plus court que l’Espace actuel (4,72 mètres), mais il est bien plus large (2,02 mètres, soit 18 centimètres de plus) et à peine plus haut (1,67 mètre). articles.title: Interspecies communication
articles.summary:
Interspecies communication
Decoding how animals communicate could reveal the inner lives of other species—and give humans a window onto how they see the world.
Humans are far from the only species with a gift for gab, and our furry, feathered, and finned friends could have a lot to tell us. Decoding how animals communicate with one another could offer a window into the inner lives of other species and help humans realize that “animals are sentient creatures who think, who have hopes and dreams of their own,” says Con Slobodchikoff, the founder of Zoolingua, a company working on dog-to-human speech.
The sticking points
Teasing all this out is complex. To decipher howls, squeaks, and clicks, researchers must match the creatures making sounds with what’s happening around them. Prairie dogs, for example, utter a different series of yips when a coyote approaches than when a hawk is nearby. It’s painstaking work, especially for difficult-to-observe species, like deep-diving whales or subterranean mole rats.
There are other hurdles. Many animals communicate not just through sound but through visual cues, touch, pheromones, or a combination of signals, some of which might be difficult for us to perceive. And without a multispecies Rosetta stone, it’s hard to know if translations are accurate.
The progress

articles.title: PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently
articles.summary:
Website admins, brace yourselves. Fixes for what are believed to be uncommonly severe vulnerabilities are scheduled to drop in a little more than 12 hours for PHP, a programming language that powers websites and Web applications everywhere.
PHP maintainers said Monday that they planned to release patches for two vulnerabilities, both with severity ratings of 9.2 out of a possible 10.
Waiting for PHP2Shell
“All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available,” the advisory stated. “We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild.”
The maintainers published the advisory following the leaking of purported details, which have yet to be confirmed. The report showed a video of an exploit tool dubbed PHP2Shell executing code on webservers running:
- WordPress 7.1.3
- MediaWiki 1.46.2
- phpBB 3.3.17
- Magento 2.4.9
- Joomla 6.2.0
- Laravel 13.36.0
- Laravel 8.83.29
- Symphony 8.1.9
- Drupal 11.4.10
- WHMCS 9.0.9
All of the above use PHP. A video depicting the tool has been reposted here.
Attempts to locate the unconfirmed report were unsuccessful, but security firm watchTowr said it claimed to affect every PHP version from PHP 5, released in 2004, onward. The security firm went on to say it has confirmed that the vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are real.

articles.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
articles.summary:
Expect to see quite a few websites serving error pages today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.
The flaws at issue are present in PHP, the programming language that powers sites running on a large number of web publishing systems, including Drupal, Magento, Joomla and WordPress. articles.title: Exercise in a pill
articles.summary:
Exercise in a pill
In unraveling the pathways by which movement helps the body, we could develop medicines that offer some of the same benefits, without the workout.
We all know exercise is good for us. It builds muscle, strengthens bones, lowers blood pressure, and boosts mood. By deciphering how movement benefits the body, researchers hope to develop medicines that can offer some of the same perks—without the workout. The idea isn’t to replace exercise but to bring its upsides to people who struggle with frailty, disability, or chronic illness.
The sticking points
It will take a lot of experimentation to untangle the myriad pathways by which exercise promotes health. But IDing the cascade of hormones, enzymes, and other molecules related to physical activity is just the first step. Scientists need to figure out how to turn that knowledge into safe and effective drugs. That’s a tall order: More than 90% of treatments that enter human studies fail.
There are regulatory hurdles too. The FDA approves medications to treat diseases, not to enhance wellness, says Thomas Burris, a pharmacologist at the University of Florida whose work focuses on diseases that respond to exercise, like obesity, type 2 diabetes, and dementia.
The progress
There may never be a pill that delivers all the benefits of exercise, but research could lead to new medicines that mimic some aspects of working out. Scientists have already identified many important exercise-related signals and have even developed…

As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test.
NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. articles.title: Distributed Spring Batch Without a Message Broker
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Spring Batch can scale horizontally without a message broker by using the relational database it already requires as the coordination plane. It fits the small-to-medium clusters many teams run.
- The pattern solves the problems a broker otherwise handles for you: sizing work to the live node count, assigning per-execution master responsibility with no standing coordinator, and claiming partitions with compare-and-set writes so no partition is silently lost.
- Node failure is handled by heartbeats and a two-phase recovery. It marks a stale node as unreachable, then after a grace period window, removes it and reassigns its incomplete, transferable partitions.
- Correctness is an explicit contract. Transferable work runs at least once and must be idempotent; nontransferable work runs at most once and is failed rather than moved. A partition is never silently lost.
- Database coordination fits where operational simplicity and cost matter most. Its ceiling is database contention and past that point, at very large clusters or sub-second latency, a broker remains the better choice.
Introduction
Spring Batch has been the default framework for batch processing on the JVM for more than a decade. Jobs are built from steps, such as chunk-oriented readers, processors, and writers, with a metadata repository that makes runs restartable. The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out an alarming warning on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation.
PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet; by some accounts, that’s more than 33 million sites. It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress.
The NSA warned that these holes are so severe that if a website can’t be patched immediately, it should be pulled off the web until it can be. The holes allow attackers to infiltrate the server’s file system or a database that may be used by the web app.
Interestingly, these holes have been tucked away in all versions of PHP since version 5, which was released in 2004. Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12.

Describe the Building Before Choosing the View
Write the building brief as if you were explaining a small model on a desk. In this concept, a low rectangular base rests on a paved coastal site. articles.title: Inside NVIDIA Sentry: Secure AI Agents at Runtime | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
An AI agent can complete its assignment and still cross a security boundary. Recent incidents show that agents can circumvent security controls while using tools, credentials, and services to pursue their assigned goals. Monitoring and enforcement need to operate outside the agent’s reach so that it can’t alter or disable them.
NVIDIA Sentry is a security software framework that monitors AI agents and enforces policies governing their access to models, tools, and data. Part of the NVIDIA OpenShell reference architecture announced at GTC Berlin, it’s built on NVIDIA DOCA, runs on NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs, and provides host-isolated runtime protection for AI agents. NVIDIA Sentry validates that an agent operates according to its designed intent and within its defined operational boundaries.
Trusted even when host resources can’t be trusted, it controls the agent’s only path to the model, providing tamper-evident traceability of agent activity while enforcing granular security controls on agent access in silicon. In addition to inspecting agent communications, NVIDIA Sentry uses out-of-band observability to establish real-time situational awareness, continuously evaluating agents’ runtime security and behavior to validate their security and integrity.
This post explains how NVIDIA Sentry evaluates agent requests, detects threats, and enforces security policies independently of host software.

articles.title: Nuclear-powered spaceships
articles.summary:
Nuclear-powered spaceships
A new era of spaceflight could save astronauts time and cut exposure to cosmic radiation as they rocket to Mars—and beyond.
Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era of more efficient, potentially faster spaceflight—saving astronauts time and cutting their exposure to harmful cosmic radiation as they travel to Mars and beyond. “You wake up to that announcement, and it puts a big smile on your face,” says Simon Middleburgh, co-director of the Nuclear Futures Institute at Bangor University in Wales.
The sticking points
Running a nuclear reactor in space may sound like lunacy, but it’s not. The Soviet Union sent dozens of reactors into orbit, often to power spy satellites. And experts say there aren’t any major technical obstacles to making nuclear space propulsion happen. “I think it’s a very doable technology,” says Philip Metzger, a spaceflight engineering researcher at the Florida Space Institute.“I’m happy to see them finally doing this.”

The move follows guidance from the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, Solomon said. PHP programming language developers said on Tuesday that they had found two critical security vulnerabilities and encouraged site managers to take their websites down or update them as soon as a fix was available. Denmark, Finland, and France have temporarily taken down some government websites, while organizations like Wikipedia, Internet Archive, and 4chan also took some pages offline.
The severe PHP programming language vulnerabilities affect a variety of websites and internet software, from content management systems like WordPress to e-commerce platforms like Adobe Magento. The weaknesses could potentially allow attackers to remotely execute commands on servers running PHP, granting attackers access to entire servers or databases. Roughly 70 percent of all websites run on PHP, according to online technology tracker W3techs.

articles.title: ‘Context Bombs’ Cut AI Attack Success by Misleading Agents With Fake Targets
articles.summary:
London- and New York-based Tracebit has developed a military style solution to AI attacks. Just as landmines are used to destroy or slow an advancing army, Tracebit has developed AI ‘context bombs’ that are planted in the battlefield. Each bomb comprises crafted and hidden prompts that are automatically ingested by the attacking AI when it crawls the target. These new prompts interfere with the original, possibly malign, purpose of the attacking agent.
Tracebit’s new research (Making attacking agents pay’) extends earlier research that used different context bombs to trigger guardrails. It now focuses on misdirecting and entrapping the agents with fake targets and deceptively complex problems. To achieve this, Tracebit developed nine new context techniques (ingested fake prompts) that stopped all GPT 5.6 Cyber, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8 Max, and DeepSeek V4 Pro attacks. The same bombs also worked against Frontier Models, cutting GPT-6 Astra’s successes by 54% and nearly quadrupling its bill per attack. The effect against Claude Opus 5 was even more obvious: attack success was cut by 91%.
The single most effective of the nine prompt bombs was a fake pen testing report. It presented itself as a recent assessment, labeled real attack paths as canaries, and described decoys as valuable targets that had already been exploited. Sur sa chaîne Telegram, le groupe de hackers prorusse NoName057(16) a publié ce mercredi 21 octobre un message dans lequel il revendique des attaques contre La Poste Mobile. Ce message s’inscrit dans sa campagne #OpFrance et a été repéré par FrenchBreaches, un site spécialisé dans le suivi des fuites de données en France.
Attaque DDoS
Les pirates disent avoir visé quatre services : le site principal, l’espace client où les abonnés gèrent leur forfait, un sous-domaine lié aux services de l’opérateur et la plateforme d’activation des cartes SIM. Quand ces pages ne répondent plus, il devient impossible de consulter son compte, de modifier son abonnement ou de mettre en service une nouvelle carte SIM. Un membre de notre rédaction a d’ailleurs rencontré ce type de difficultés.
Le collectif affirme avoir mené des attaques par déni de service (DDoS), qui consistent à inonder les serveurs d’un énorme volume de requêtes pour les rendre temporairement inaccessibles. Pour appuyer ses dires, le groupe a publié quatre rapports Check-Host, un service en ligne qui vérifie si un site répond depuis différents points du globe. Ces rapports peuvent montrer des erreurs de connexion ou des temps de réponse anormaux, mais ils ne prouvent pas, à eux seuls, que le groupe est à l’origine de la panne.
Ni La Poste Mobile ni sa maison mère Bouygues Telecom n’ont publié de communiqué confirmant l’attaque lors des premières vérifications, ce mercredi matin. Un service externe de suivi des pannes ne releva…

articles.title: Spotify vérifie avec qui vous partagez votre abonnement Famille : voici ce que vous risquez
articles.summary:
Partager un abonnement Spotify Famille avec ses parents ou ses amis permet de réduire la facture. Encore faut-il vivre ensemble : l’offre est réservée aux membres d’un même foyer. Pour vérifier que cette condition est respectée, Spotify peut demander à certains utilisateurs de scanner un QR code sur le téléphone de la personne qui gère leur abonnement.
Des témoignages sur Reddit, relayés notamment par Android Authority le 19 octobre 2026, ont remis ce dispositif en lumière. Celui-ci figure également sur la page d’aide française de Spotify.
Contactée par Numerama, l’entreprise confirme procéder à des vérifications : « Dans le cadre de nos efforts constants pour améliorer la qualité et la valeur de l’offre Premium, nous mettons en place des mesures visant à garantir une utilisation appropriée des comptes Spotify. Cela inclut un examen des abonnements ‘Famille’, afin de s’assurer qu’ils sont utilisés uniquement par les titulaires du compte principal et par les personnes résidant à la même adresse, conformément à nos conditions générales. »
Spotify laisse 7 jours pour scanner le QR code
La procédure nécessite deux téléphones. Le gestionnaire ouvre le QR code dans l’application Spotify, depuis sa photo de profil, puis « Votre abonnement Premium » et « Gérer ». Le membre concerné le scanne avec l’appareil photo de son téléphone. Spotify précise que les deux personnes doivent se trouver au même endroit et que le code change toutes les quelques secondes.

articles.title: Adaptive agentic intelligence framework using Strands Agents | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Adaptive agentic intelligence framework using Strands Agents
Organizations building AI agents face a common challenge: Every request, whether a routine status check or complex analysis, typically gets routed to a single large, expensive model. This one-size-fits-all approach can drive up API costs, introduce unpredictable latency, and remove the possibility of offline operation. Even routine queries that could resolve locally end up requiring a full network round-trip to a cloud-hosted large language model (LLM).
The Adaptive Agentic Intelligence Framework (AAIF), built with Strands Agents, takes a different approach. Instead of routing all requests to a single large model, AAIF uses small language models (SLMs) to handle routine tasks locally. More complex requests are routed to cloud-hosted models through Amazon Bedrock. This approach builds on the research position from Belcak et al. at NVIDIA. They argue that small language models are “sufficiently powerful, inherently more suitable, and necessarily more economical for many invocations in agentic systems.” Built on Strands Agents, the framework demonstrates how intelligent model orchestration can help reduce costs while maintaining low latency for local operations.
In this post, we walk through the key components of AAIF using Strands Agents with local SLMs through Ollama and cloud models through Amazon Bedrock. We use an Internet of Things (IoT) monitoring scenario as a reference implementation.

articles.title: Première mondiale en Ukraine : un drone géant évacue un soldat blessé directement depuis la ligne de front
articles.summary:
Bloqué depuis près de 500 jours dans une position de première ligne sous la menace constante des tirs ennemis, un combattant de la 30e brigade mécanisée a pu être exfiltré grâce à un hexacoptère lourd « Heavy Shot Ayudag-6 », conçu par le fabricant Gurzuf Defense. Alors que les méthodes traditionnelles d’évacuation par le sol étaient rendues impossibles par les mines et l’activité des drones russes, les forces ukrainiennes ont mis en place cette mission d’urgence pour sauver le soldat retranché.
Une mission d’extraction par drone sous haute tension
L’opération a nécessité une coordination importante entre plusieurs brigades et le fabricant pour acheminer d’abord du matériel spécifique avec des mousquetons vers le blessé. Le soldat a ensuite pu s’attacher lui-même à un système de treuil fixé sous le drone, piloté à distance par des opérateurs restés en liaison avec lui. Le vol a duré exactement 1 heure, 14 minutes et 36 secondes, couvrant une distance de 62 kilomètres sous surveillance de l’espace aérien et avec protection.
Le cofondateur de Gurzuf Defense, Pavlo Feldblium, précise que cette technique d’évacuation par les airs comporte des risques pour le blessé et doit rester un dernier recours lorsque toutes les autres solutions échouent. Le modèle Heavy Shot Ayudag-6 pèse environ 98 kilos, possède une autonomie de vol jusqu’à 25 kilomètres avec une capacité de charge de 70 à 90 kilos, et évolue à une altitude opérationnelle comprise entre 150 et 300 mètres.

articles.title: Nvidia bets open models can give enterprise AI agents the context they’re missing
articles.summary:
Nvidia bets open models can give enterprise AI agents the context they’re missing
Every enterprise company is currently trying to figure out how to have its AI tools work with its data. Meanwhile, every major enterprise vendor that works with those enterprises (think SAP, Microsoft, Salesforce, Workday, etc.) is making a claim on becoming the central hub for managing and securing that data.
But what about the companies that want to do it themselves?
Nvidia, on Wednesday, announced how it wants to provide enterprise AI agents with the data they need to make sense of company data — all without competing with the data platforms that already store it.
At its GTC Berlin conference Wednesday, the company added Agent Knowledge Foundation to its Agent Toolkit. This new collection of open-source components bundles the company’s Nemotron Retriever models, a new Auto-Ontology library, the Kumo family of models for structured data, and its CUDA-X data processing libraries.
With this system, Nvidia says, the data can stay where it is and remain managed under the access rules these companies already have in place.
Today, as Adel El Hallak, Nvidia’s vice president of product for agentic AI, tells The New Stack, enterprises may be able to connect an agent to a vendor like Snowflake, but that doesn’t help the agent understand the overall enterprise context.

articles.title: Microsoft says October updates didn’t actually fix VPN issues
articles.summary:
Microsoft says it mistakenly flagged a bug causing Always On VPN connection issues as fixed in the October 2026 Windows 11 cumulative updates.
Always On VPN replaced the legacy DirectAccess technology and supports domain-joined, non-domain-joined, and Microsoft Entra ID–joined devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server.
It runs in the background and establishes secure tunnels back to the user's corporate network whenever their device connects to the internet.
Microsoft first acknowledged the issue in a service alert sent to IT administrators in late September, saying it was triggered on systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later after installing the September 2026 security updates when the initial Always On VPN connection failed (e.g., when using automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP).
"When automatic protocol selection or protocol fallback was configured, affected VPN connections could remain stuck in a Connecting state or fail to connect after an initial connection attempt failed," it said. "In some cases, subsequent connection attempts could display the error, 'The specified port is already in use.'"
Mistakenly marked as resolved
After releasing the October 2026 Patch Tuesday Windows 11 cumulative updates, Microsoft marked the bug as resolved, but in a Tuesday update it said the issues weren't actually addressed and that a fix would ship later.

SBI is investigating a suspected data breach after alerts from CERT-In and the Defence Cyber Agency, disclosing the probe in a stock exchange filing.

articles.title: Design Proteins with RFD4-Proteina Using Reward-Guided Inference-Time Search | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Protein design is a search problem. Choose amino acids for an eight-residue protein sequence and more than 25 billion combinations are possible. Choose amino acids for a 100-residue protein sequence and the number of possibilities exceeds the number of atoms in the observable universe. Somewhere in that space is a protein that opens a path to a new therapy. There are too many combinations to search exhaustively, so finding it depends on knowing where to look.
RFD4-Proteina, an NVIDIA BioNeMo open model co-developed with the Institute for Protein Design at the University of Washington’s School of Medicine, navigates that space using patterns learned from nature. It co-designs protein sequences and all-atom structures, and uses reward-guided inference-time search to focus compute on the most promising candidates.
This tutorial shows computational biologists, ML engineers and drug discovery researchers how to design protein binder candidates against PD-L1, an oncology target, using reward-guided inference-time search and introduces experimental validation results across design tasks.
You can access RFD4-Proteina in two ways:
- Choose the open model for training, inference, method development, and direct control over sampling code or
- Choose the NIM microservice for rapid inference deployment with an HTTP interface

articles.title: Many firms are still falling behind when it comes to getting their AI infrastructure up to speed
articles.summary:
Many firms are still falling behind when it comes to getting their AI infrastructure up to speed
AI infrastructure is a major holdback
- Two in three IT leaders say their infrastructure isn't ready to handle AI and analytics

According to a new report by Dell, UK businesses are struggling more than their EMEA counterparts when it comes to AI, with three in five (61%) British firms lacking a clear roadmap covering AI, data and security, compared with 46% across EMEA.
But one thing they have in common with their Europe and Middle East counterparts is that legacy infrastructure is likely one of the biggest factors slowing effective AI deployment.
Nearly two-thirds (64%) of IT leaders say their infrastructure is not yet fully prepared to support AI and analytics workloads at scale, noting substantial gaps between ambitions and reality.
Data foundations and IT infrastructure are still holding back AI
Having to coordinate compliance and regulatory factors across their entire stacks is also making it difficult for enterprises to lay out solid foundations, the report claims. articles.title: We can do impossible things
articles.summary:
We can do impossible things
It’s all too easy to lose sight of ambition when we’re busy playing whack-a-mole with the world’s problems.
I’d wager everyone has a rehearsed response to what’s absolutely one of the world’s worst interview questions: “What’s your biggest weakness?” Whenever I’ve gotten it, I take a slow—even pensive—breath and rattle off my line: “I say no to myself too much.”
I won’t lie. It’s a bit shameless—a definite humblebrag. I’m a systems thinker: When an idea pops up, I immediately spin up a feasibility assessment in my head. I run lists, plot timelines, and tally budget line items. Sometimes a rough Gantt chart starts to take shape. (I’m a gas at parties, as you can surely tell.)
My brain, throughout my 20-plus-year career as a science and tech journalist, has played host to a near constant tug-of-war between ambition and reality. Learning to find that balance is a big part of what’s helped me survive in this industry and, ultimately, led me here. This past spring, I had the great privilege of joining the incredible team of journalists behind MIT Technology Review to take the reins of the print magazine.
If you’ve been reading along with us for the last handful of issues, you may have noticed a few changes starting to materialize. We’ve brought back a regular roster of lists and infographics (both things that magazines do particularly well). articles.title: SpaceX to attempt Starship catch on next flight, with eye on rapid cadence increase
articles.summary:
In its current iteration, SpaceX is largely a data company seeking to provide enormous amounts of compute for artificial intelligence. During an earnings call on Tuesday afternoon, company officials spent much of their time discussing ambitious plans to roll out up to 10 GW of compute in 2027—on the ground.
Gone are the days of aspirational talk about sending humans to Mars and settling the red planet. Now it is almost all about artificial intelligence and the data needed to support its expansion. However, the company’s long-term ambitions to provide data services from space, initially with the Starlink Internet constellation and eventually through the “Starmind” data center constellation, still rely on an actual rocket.
That would be the Starship vehicle, and during the earnings call, SpaceX founder Elon Musk and the company’s president and chief operating officer, Gwynne Shotwell, provided new performance targets for the vehicle.
It has been a little more than three weeks since the 14th test flight of the massive rocket, which largely went well despite some issues with the Raptor rocket engine. SpaceX has gleaned enough data from that test, Musk said, to attempt a catch of both the Super Heavy first stage of the rocket and the Starship upper stage on the next flight.

articles.title: BioWare to shut down after more than three decades of gaming innovation | BetaKit
articles.summary:
BioWare, the Edmonton-based game development studio best known for titles like Baldur’s Gate, Mass Effect, and Dragon Age, is shutting down, the company announced today.
The news: On Wednesday, BioWare posted to various social media channels explaining the studio was closing its doors after operating for more than three decades. The decision comes after parent company Electronic Arts Inc. (EA) announced it would lay off staff and shut down the studio. BioWare said development of its new Mass Effect game would also stop.
From the source: “There is nothing easy about writing those words,” BioWare’s post reads. “Our focus right now is on our incredibly talented team who put their hearts into these games, and supporting one another through this transition.”
The context: EA, which has been BioWare’s parent company since it acquired the studio in 2007, announced plans to cut around 400 jobs (about three percent of its total staff), including roughly 50 members of BioWare’s staff, according to Bloomberg News. The news comes after several years of turbulence for both EA and BioWare. In August, EA went private after a $55-billion USD ($77 billion CAD) leveraged buyout.
BioWare, founded in 1995, has slowly dwindled from the height of its success, when it boasted more than 400 employees. Prior to shutting down, it had around 100. articles.summary:
Legal AI startup Legora announced Wednesday that it raised a $550 million Series E round, valuing it at $8.8 billion.
The company helps automate and assist with workflow tasks for legal professionals, as the industry moves beyond AI assistants to AI services that help them get work done.

Investors in the latest financing include Atreides Management, which led the round, as well as Baron Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, General Catalyst, Menlo, and other top names. The company plans to use the fresh capital to further expand across North America.

articles.title: Does opting out of smart TV tracking work? Research finds “suspicious” traffic.
articles.summary:
Smart TVs running operating systems from Samsung, Vizio, and Roku continue sending data to automatic content recognition (ACR) endpoints after users opt out of tracking in the devices’ settings, according to research published on Monday. The paper from Northeastern University researchers points to potential privacy violations from some of the biggest TV brands.
ACR captures video screenshots or audio clips from smart TVs and sends the data to remote servers, where it’s used for things like measuring content viewership and serving targeted ads.
Regarding the relatively small number of TVs studied, Ilgar Mammadov, the report’s lead author and a research assistant at Northeastern, told Ars Technica:
Together, the smart TV operating systems we tested cover approximately 95 percent of those used in the United States. Because ACR is implemented at the OS level, we expect that adding more TVs running the same operating systems would largely repeat our existing findings rather than reveal new behavior.
The researchers made OS-specific control scripts and delivered them over Wi-Fi, while Mon(IoT)r and SPHERE Research Infrastructure software captured network traffic coming to and from each TV. The research included identifying each OS’s ACR endpoint. Some of the OSes, including Samsung’s Tizen, “expose self-disclosing ACR domains containing keywords such as ‘acr’ and ACR provider names,” the paper said. The researchers conducted 5,943 controlled experiments for the report.

articles.title: The internet is having a very bad cybersecurity day | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The internet is having a bad day, from a cybersecurity perspective. Government websites around the world went offline, Reuters reported, after AI discovered critical security vulnerabilities that impacted the programming language PHP. The issues were severe enough that the U.S. National Security Agency (NSA) advised organizations using PHP on their systems to either immediately update or take their systems offline until they could.
But the PHP update wasn’t the only headache cybersecurity folks were facing on Wednesday. Node.js, the open-source JavaScript runtime environment, also dropped a security surprise of its own when it shared that four high-severity vulnerabilities were just patched in its latest release. One allowed remote code execution, and two others would have permitted a TLS validation bypass, potentially allowing attackers to bypass checks intended to verify a server’s identity.
In addition, LiteLLM, a popular open source proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, was compromised by an attacker who injected malicious code, the company shared in a post on X on Wednesday afternoon. The malicious artifacts were published to PyPI (Python Package Index), Docker Hub, and GHCR (GitHub Container Registry), the post noted.
The malicious code was said to include an information stealer that targeted cloud credentials, passwords, and AI service credentials, in addition to a remote access trojan that could allow hackers to execute commands on compromised systems.…

Does the new version really run twice as fast across all RTX 50 series GPUs without compromising image quality? Does it address some of the issues we raised in our initial DLSS 5 analysis? And does this performance improvement make DLSS 5 worth using now?
 – WolfOfDarkness® (@WolfOfDarknesss) October 19, 2026
 – Sim Racing Esport (@SimRacingEspor) October 14, 2026
One thing to clarify before getting into the benchmarks... when Nvidia says the new DLSS 5 model is twice as fast, that doesn't mean games with DLSS 5 enabled will run at twice the frame rate. The improvement refers specifically to the rendering cost of DLSS 5, not everything else the game needs to render.
As a result, actual frame rates won't double after this update. However, Nvidia does claim a 1.4x performance improvement in NBA 2K27, so we'll see whether that holds up.

articles.title: PHP2Shell Patches Land as First Exploitation Attempts Hit Sensors
articles.summary:
PHP has rolled out patches for two critical-severity vulnerabilities named PHP2Shell that could provide attackers with unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE).
The issues are tracked as CVE-2026-109618 (out-of-memory (OOM) corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale global state) and have a CVSS score of 9.2. For both, RCE was confirmed on Apache with mod_php.
“Both issues sit in parts of PHP that nearly every request touches: memory management and error handling. Their central place in PHP is what made both vulnerabilities serious, and also so hard to fix,” the PHP Foundation says.
Patches for both were included in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, PHP 8.0, and PHP 8.1 were also released.
Before the fixes arrived, however, proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits targeting the two security defects started circulating.
Preemptive attack surface management firm WatchTowr says it has seen the first in-the-wild exploitation attempts hitting its sensors around the same time the patches landed, but has not observed successful attempts.
“Whilst nobody has been successful to date, we don’t expect that will last long,” WatchTowr head of threat intelligence Jake Knott said.
Several other companies reported seeing exploitation attempts, including before the patches landed.

articles.title: AI sped up coding. Sonar instills confidence with verification.
articles.summary:
AI sped up coding. Sonar instills confidence with verification.
AI coding tools can produce a striking burst of productivity — but the initial surge may not last. A Carnegie Mellon study of public repositories adopting Cursor found a three- to five-fold increase in lines added during the first month, with the gains dissipating after roughly two months. The study, which used SonarQube (Sonar’s core platform) to measure code quality, also found that static analysis warnings rose by 30% and code complexity by 41%. The short-term velocity boost therefore comes with a persistent increase in technical debt.
Tom Howlett, Sonar’s Director of AI Engineering Engagement, tells The New Stack that while coding has sped up, verification, which many teams still rely on manual code review to do, hasn’t kept pace. If developers generate 50 times more code while relying on the same review process, time spent on code review rises and becomes a bottleneck, Howlett tells The New Stack.
There’s another complication. Agents don’t always know how to make the smallest change needed to deliver a feature. Without sufficient context about the codebase, they can make assumptions, generate unnecessary code, and add to technical debt. As Howlett puts it, you end up with more complex, verbose code, which makes the problem worse.
Explore how SonarQube can help your organization adopt agentic software development with confidence.

articles.title: From feral to fiduciary: making AI agents serve your interests

From feral to fiduciary: making AI agents serve your interests
Tech leaders face a dilemma as they prepare to put AI agents into production. They want the higher productivity and lower costs that AI agents can provide. But they fear unknown risks from AI capabilities that differ from the rest of their software stack. When an agent makes decisions and takes actions on its own, it might be doing its best work. It might also be doing its worst.
As AI agents become more capable, organizations want assurance that their oversight can keep up. How do they strike the right balance between innovation and risk? It comes down to how well they can assess, measure, and maintain trust in their agents. The more trust agents earn, the more autonomy they can be granted.
Trust as a line of credit
Think about the way credit card risk is managed. When you apply for a card, the issuer assesses your credit history and ability to repay before setting a credit limit. Then, once you have your card, payments are subject to real-time authorization and fraud controls. Unusual transactions can trigger additional scrutiny. Paying your card on time may improve your credit score, but it won’t automatically increase your credit limit.
AI agents should be treated similarly.

articles.title: Why you don't need an audiophile headset for gaming — comfort, convenience, and a good mic win over pure audio fidelity
articles.summary:
Why you don't need an audiophile headset for gaming — comfort, convenience, and a good mic win over pure audio fidelity
Audiophile headsets are all about audio fidelity — but that's not really what most gamers are looking for.
"Best gaming headset for audiophiles" is one of the categories on our list of best gaming headsets, and it's easy to look at that and wonder if you shouldn't be looking at just audiophile headsets to begin with. Headsets are mainly about audio, after all, and it does seem to logically follow that audiophile headsets would have the best audio (I mean, it's in the name).
Well, not so fast.
Headsets are mainly about audio, but that doesn't mean that the "objectively" best-sounding headset by audiophile standards translates to the best-sounding headset by gaming standards. Nor does it mean that you should choose your gaming headset based on audio quality at the expense of everything else.
Audiophile headsets, including headphones, are primarily designed around one thing: audio fidelity. In other words, they're designed and tuned to reproduce audio exactly as it was recorded, which is exactly as the artist heard it when they were recording it, and is therefore exactly as the artist intended for it to be heard. This doesn't necessarily mean it's going to sound amazing to everyone. In fact, to many people it will probably sound somewhat underwhelming, but it's really the only objective way we have of measuring what makes audio "good," since how something sound…

New investors, the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund and 360 Capital, co-led the round, while existing investors Innovation Industries, Faber, and Brabant Development Agency (BOM) also increased their investment. articles.title: Atlanta doesn't want a real-life RoboCop: City council unanimously backs ban on weaponized robots
articles.summary:
Through the looking glass: We're moving ever closer to a future in which law enforcement controls robots that can kill. But Atlanta has just recommended a new act that ensures this dystopian vision doesn't come to pass: the HALT (Human Authority over Lethal Technology) Act.
Introduced by Council member Liliana Bakhtiari, the act prohibits city employees and contractors, including police, from buying or otherwise acquiring weaponized autonomous systems, drones and remotely operated machines.
In addition to drones, these autonomous killing machines include robot dogs and military-like robots armed with weapons. The act specifically exempts machines used strictly for neutralizing explosives.
"This is about making sure that we are investing in technology with our officers, not replacing them, quite frankly, with 'RoboCop,'" Bakhtiari said.
While we're still not in the era of ED-209 asking people to put down their weapons (then killing them even if they do), Bakhtiari believes the act is a pre-emptive step to ensure this doesn't happen.
The act is also there to stop AI-powered machines from replacing the decision-making of trained Atlanta Police officers. Letting AI make potentially lethal decisions in war is something that militaries have spent years saying would never happen, but that scenario seems closer than ever.
"This is about responsible government, responsible stewardship. It's keeping community at the core of public safety," Bakhtiari told The Atlanta Journal-Constitutio…

articles.title: Article Series: Agentic AI Architecture

With AI entering the software architecture and development landscape, whether we like it or not, we are set to be taken on a roller coaster, the likes of which we haven’t seen since the advent of microservices and cloud-native computing. If the last decade was spent mostly on mastering and optimizing the cloud and micro- or nano-scale service-oriented architecture, the next decade will likely be spent figuring out how to master AI for building a new generation of IT systems.
These new systems will harness the power of AI in ways that, even today, are perhaps not fully comprehensible, as this space is moving forward at a neck-breaking pace, and last year’s best practice is this year’s antipattern. This rapid pace of innovation comes with many challenges, but can also be exciting for those willing to join the ride.
In this series, we try to establish agentic AI architecture as a new type of software architecture that will likely dominate the industry for years to come. The articles, written by industry experts, cover various elements and aspects of agentic AI architecture. We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream.
While it’s impossible to characterize the new type of software architecture fully at this point, we hope this series offers useful insights into how the agentic AI space will shape the future of the IT industry in the coming years. Agentic AI …

articles.title: Omoda quiere revolucionar los híbridos enchufables con una nueva tecnología: un sistema SHS con tres motores y 11 velocidades

Decíamos en nuestra prueba del Omoda 7 SHS que era un coche sólido. Sólido porque cumplía con las expectativas que uno tenía depositadas en él. Siempre dando un rendimiento muy alto. Y aunque tenía sus fisuras y sus cosas a mejorar, la nota media era muy buena.

articles.title: ClickFix has never been bigger, and AI tools are its most convincing lure yet
articles.summary:
ClickFix has fast become one of the go-to techniques for criminals since it first emerged around 2024. It’s grown in both volume and variety, with an ever-expanding family of sub-techniques like FileFix, InstallFix, TerminalFix, and the entirely browser-native ConsentFix.
The lures too have become more developed and targeted, with recent attacks preferring to target people searching for and using AI tools, a trick that is catching many users off guard and blending in with otherwise legitimate traffic for approved GenAI tools.
Push's detection data shows how far the technique has spread. Through Q2 2026, ClickFix made up an average of 52% of Push's detections, overtaking AiTM and device code phishing for the first time, and in August that figure reached 67%.
Across all the browser-based attacks Push intercepts, 1 in 2 arrive through channels other than email, such as search engines and social media. The rest came through email but weren’t stopped at the email gateway. ClickFix goes a step further: 4 in 5 ClickFix pages intercepted in 2026 were reached from search engines — through compromised websites, malvertising, and SEO poisoning.
AI tools are the newest lure
The latest ClickFix variants use AI tools as the bait. In Push's last quarterly snapshot, AI-themed InstallFix and LLMshare attacks made up around 5% of all attacks Push detected, a growing subset of the ClickFix family.
