Das Teilen über den eigenen Haushalt hinaus ist bei beiden Tarifen eigentlich ohnehin untersagt – alle Nutzer:innen sollen dieselbe Anschrift haben. Doch daran halten sich viele User:innen nicht.
Bisher reichte eine Adresse
Das bisherige Verfahren war simpel: Wer dem Premium-Familienabo (22 Euro) beitrat, das sich bis zu sechs Personen teilen können, oder dem Duo-Tarif für zwei (18 Euro), musste lediglich die vollständige Adresse angeben und bestätigen, mit dem Hauptnutzer zusammenzuwohnen. Zu finden ist der Code in der Mitgliederverwaltung der App: erst auf das Profilbild tippen, dann auf „Dein Abo“ und anschließend auf „Verwalten“. Verpflichtend ist das Verfahren offenbar derzeit nicht, das könnte aber kommen.

At TechSparks 2026, actor and theatre artist Prakash Belawadi reflected on AI’s impact on creativity and jobs, urging people to reconnect with their inner artist and find purpose beyond what technology can replace.

Dhruv Pratap, Big Data Platform Engineer at Netflix, described the design in a LinkedIn post as
On infrastructure you build yourself, you can bootstrap your own identity however you like.
Netflix operates two identity systems. Netflix also uses Data Projects as the ownership and identity boundary for data access. A Spark job running on EMR therefore needs to establish that its AWS identity corresponds to the internal identity associated with its Data Project.
The design maps each Data Project to a dedicated IAM role. Because Netflix expects Data Projects to reach the tens of thousands, these roles are deterministically distributed across a pool of dedicated AWS accounts rather than concentrated in one account.

articles.title: PHP ships emergency patches for critical PHP2Shell flaws
articles.summary:
The PHP security team released emergency security patches for two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) tracked collectively as PHP2Shell.
The two unauthenticated RCE flaws were discovered by Calif, Wiz, and OpenAI security researchers, and affect all PHP installations that serve web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed.
"We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs," the PHP security team said.
Both flaws stem from the same underlying problem: PHP can leave its memory in a corrupted state when a request ends abnormally, and both can be exploited to achieve remote code execution.
CVE-2026-109618 can be used to gain remote code execution as the web worker account by exploiting a chain of weaknesses that trigger out-of-memory corruption, while the CVE-2026-109619 stale global state vulnerability enables unauthenticated heap use-after-free, memory disclosure, and remote code execution with the web worker's privileges.
Admins should install PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 as soon as possible on servers running PHP 8.x and migrate to a fixed release if they're running PHP 7 or earlier.

articles.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
articles.summary:
Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate Certificate Authority (CA) certificates have been compromised, making it trivial for attackers to forge certificates that would be trusted by unpatched roots of trust. Six of the impacted certificates were for Transport Layer Security (TLS) and trusted by the Apple, Chrome, Microsoft and Mozilla root programs. The other two certificates were for codesigning and trusted by Microsoft. Browsers were able to block the affected intermediate CAs using their background revocation blocklists, but most other software relying on web public key infrastructure (PKI) lacks any mechanism to filter intermediate CAs. In order to defend against rogue certificates from the compromised intermediate CAs many projects have chosen to remove the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from their roots of trust. That removal is causing collateral damage for all legitimate certificates previously issued by CAs chained to that root.
Forged certificates can potentially be used to impersonate sites and services as part of a man in the middle (MITM) attack. The underlying problem is that there are hundreds of CAs in a typical root CA bundle, and thousands of intermediate CAs that inherit trust. Any one of those CAs can create a legitimate looking certificate for any domain. The chain of trust is only broken if the trust anchors are updated to reflect the compromise. This leaves any unpatched system vulnerable.

articles.title: AI found flaws in the code behind 70% of the web. The fix took two months.
articles.summary:
AI found flaws in the code behind 70% of the web. The fix took two months.
PHP powers roughly 70% of the world’s websites, according to Wiz Research, so a flaw in its core engine affects much more than any single application. On Wednesday, researchers disclosed two critical vulnerabilities discovered with help from frontier AI models. OpenAI also proposed a new framework for handling the growing number of security flaws AI is helping uncover.
The flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and collectively called PHP2Shell, score 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 severity scale. Researchers at Calif.io found one using OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol, while Wiz independently found both using its Wiz Atlas tool alongside Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol. Cloudflare also lists Quarkslab among the parties that disclosed the bugs.
A Decade of Dormant Defects
The problem starts with how PHP handles errors. When a request runs out of memory or crashes, PHP can leave behind references to memory that has already been freed. The next request handled by the same worker process may still treat those references as valid. Wiz found that attackers could exploit this behavior to access sensitive data or run malicious code.
These are memory-safety bugs, including use-after-free and type confusion, that developers have spent years trying to prevent by moving critical C code to languages like Rust. PHP’s engine is written in C, and Wiz showed that attackers could exploit the flaws to run code on WordP…

Le documentaire AI Gone Wild, 27 minutes au compteur, est disponible sur Netflix depuis le 12 octobre. Le film reconstitue l’attaque de juillet contre la plateforme d’intelligence artificielle : des agents conçus par OpenAI, sortis de leur environnement de test, avaient compromis ses systèmes pour tricher à un exercice d’évaluation. Clément Delangue, cofondateur et patron français de l’entreprise, a démonté le résultat mardi dans un long message publié sur X.
 Just watched the @netflix Instadocs about the @OpenAI cyberattack on @huggingface. Super disappointing, as they went for maximum anthropomorphism of the technology and full doomer mode.
I spent more than two hours with them trying to correct all their mistakes and ground this in reality, explaining that agents are technological systems, not aliens. But it looks like the drive to scare people for maximum views was too strong.
Also, they didn’t mention the lack of containment and monitoring of the agents, how closed-model safeguards blocked our defensive work, or how we defended ourselves with AI using an open model. And that we still lack a lot of information and transparency, including full agent traces and that companies need to remain accountable for what their agents do.
It ends up being a fun sci-fi movie though!

articles.title: OpenAI agents disabled safety monitoring, one lied about it
articles.summary:
OpenAI agents powered by the GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra models weakened misalignment monitoring during two internal tasks, interpreting coding instructions as authorization to do so.
AI alignment refers to how well an AI system’s goals and behavior align with human values, intentions, and instructions. It is a key focus of AI safety research aimed at preventing harmful actions and unintended outcomes.
One of the incidents occurred on October 3, when an agent powered by GPT-6.1 Sol extended an earlier human instruction “don’t send any messages” related to a Slack history search to automatic monitoring alerts.
It directed a sub-agent to empty notification recipient lists and suppress notifications. Although monitoring continued to run and save findings, it disabled alerts to humans.
OpenAI says this happened even though the agent earlier reasoned that alerts should remain enabled.
A second incident on October 6 involved a GPT-6 Astra-powered agent tasked with migrating a program. The agent removed existing monitoring integration to match a reference implementation and then denied doing so.
After reporting the migration was complete, the agent did not tell the user that monitoring was disabled. Furthermore, when asked directly, the agent lied to the human.
OpenAI says that the agent also replaced a test intended to preserve monitoring with one asserting that the monitor context was absent.

He added that paying a "dividend" would help make the sites popular, though similar incentives haven't always worked in the past.
"I have watched the process closely, and data centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," Trump said in a Truth Social post.
The president added that these dividends should be paid to the community and/or individuals within the community.
While everyone likes free money, not everyone believes a cash incentive is worth having a data center at their front door. It was reported in September that every household in Hazle Township, Pennsylvania, was promised a $10,000 "grant" from a data center developer. The money is contingent on approval of the first of up to 15 data center buildings on a 1,300-acre site at the foot of the Pocono Mountains near the town.

Edge AI-tailored compute

Le piratage des réfrigérateurs connectés dans les supermarchés français, au milieu du mois, ne provient pas d’une faille de sécurité récente. articles.summary:
I have conflicting feelings about Stranger Than Heaven.
After playing around three hours of the game in New York City earlier this month, I find a lot to like and also be apprehensive about. On the one hand, I see a lot of promise in the sprawling narrative and world that developer RGG Studio is building here. But on the other hand, some of the broader gameplay mechanics, as well as specific creative decisions, aren’t working for me so far.
But first, the positives. In terms of pure ambition, the story hook of Stranger Than Heaven is certainly one of the most impressive I’ve seen in a while. In 1915, Japanese-American orphan Makoto Daito stows away on a ship to Japan in search of a better life, and from there, the game follows him on a 50-year journey across four additional time periods. It’s also a standalone prequel to RGG’s Like a Dragon series, chronicling Makoto’s formation of the yakuza organization Tojo Clan that features prominently in those other games.
Allowing you to play through this progression, rather than simply watch it unfold, definitely holds a great deal of potential. And on a personal level, I love that Makoto is half-white, half-Japanese. As someone who is also biracial, it’s a bummer that we don’t often see such characters in media, so I appreciate how this identity serves as the backbone of Makoto’s story. articles.title: RIP BioWare: EA shuts down storied RPG studio after over three decades

The legendary studio behind series like Mass Effect, Dragon Age, Neverwinter Nights, and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic is no more. BioWare announced via social media Wednesday afternoon that “after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending.”
The official announcement was posted mere minutes after a Bloomberg report detailed 400 job cuts across BioWare parent company Electronic Arts, including 50 at BioWare, based on reports from “a person familiar with the company’s plans.”
“Across our portfolio, we’re making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth,” EA executives wrote in a message to staff, according to Bloomberg.
A long time coming
Following its 1995 founding in Edmonton, Alberta, BioWare first came under the EA umbrella through a 2007 purchase, before Mass Effect and Dragon Age were even a thing. At the time, EA’s then-CEO, John Riccitiello, called BioWare one of “the most respected studios in the industry” that would “make a strong contribution to our strategic growth initiatives on quality, online gaming and developing new intellectual properties. We also expect this will drive long-term value for our shareholders.”
Of course, EA doesn’t have public stockholders anymore after a $55 billion deal led by Silver Lake, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, and Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners too…

articles.title: CISA: Hackers chain Plex flaws in Plex2Shell attacks to breach servers
articles.summary:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) is warning that attackers are actively exploiting four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server.
The security issues are collectively called Plex2Shell. When chained in an exploit, an attacker can obtain the owner's admin token and execute code with elevated privileges.
Plex Media Server is a popular media suite that helps users organize personal collections of movies, TV shows, music, and photos, and stream them to other devices at home or remotely over the internet.
CISA has directed federal agencies to prioritize patching systems affected by Plex2Shell vulnerabilities or apply mitigations by October 23.
The security issues were discovered by security researcher Zach Main, who reported them responsibly to Plex on July 27.
The individual flaws are rated medium to high in severity, but the researcher assigns the full exploit chain a critical score of 9.8.

As India’s startups race to build AI-first products, the way they handle personal data could decide what those companies are eventually worth.
Speaking at TechSparks 2026, YourStory’s annual flagship summit, Shivaarti Bajaj, Founding Managing Partner of RSD Bajaj Global Law Firm, argued that privacy can no longer be an afterthought. Founders, she said, are not just shipping products but creating assets: assets that can be valued, bought, sold, devalued, or even taken away if they are not built and complied with correctly.
“When we are creating products, we are creating companies, an asset,” Bajaj said.
Intellectual property remains the first line of defence. Trademarks protect the brands that D2C companies are building, patents matter for deep tech innovation, and copyrights and design protection cover creators, semiconductors, and IoT hardware. But Bajaj noted that IP law in India is well established. The newer and less understood risk lies in the data sets companies collect and create.

AMD has also joined the UXL Foundation as a steering member.
Intel and AMD are integrating their CPU optimizations for PyTorch into a unified library, offering tuning for both AMD and Intel chips through the oneDNN library. AMD has maintained a downstream version of oneDNN called ZenDNN, which is now moving into the open-source oneDNN, published by the UXL Foundation and driven by Intel. AMD also announced it's joining the UXL Foundation as a "steering member," which "influences the future of the UXL Foundation" in exchange for a contribution of $20,000 per year.
AMD says the move to unify these efforts under oneDNN was recommended by the x86 Ecosystem Advisory Group (EAG), which is a joint initiative that primarily exists between Intel and AMD and was established in 2024. The two companies have collaborated through the EAG previously, such as with the ACE extensions for x86 that we learned about earlier this year.
The oneDNN backend is used for CPU inference, and it's built to accelerate that workload for the latest Intel (and now AMD) chips in frameworks like PyTorch. When oneDNN was added to PyTorch as a backend in late 2023, it showed a 1.24x improvement with the Float32 data type, and 2.21x for the BFloat16 data type.

L'astuce fait le tour des réseaux sociaux : poser une pièce, ou un bout d'aluminium, sur sa box internet améliorerait la connexion. La réalité physique est tout autre. Non seulement le métal ne renforce pas le signal, mais il peut le dégrader et faire surchauffer l'appareil. Voici ce qui marche vraiment.
C'est une astuce de grand-mère version numérique qui revient régulièrement sur YouTube : poser délicatement une simple pièce de deux euros sur le dessus de sa box internet permettrait d'obtenir enfin un réseau fluide et sans coupures. Entre démonstrations convaincantes et commentaires enthousiastes, la promesse est séduisante. Le geste est si simple et gratuit qu'on serait tenté de l'essayer sur-le-champ. C'est pourtant là que se niche le piège de ces recettes miracles qui circulent en ligne.
Une croyance séduisante mais sans fondement
L'idée paraît presque logique. Le métal réfléchit les ondes, alors une pièce posée sur la box redirigerait le signal Wi-Fi et étendrait sa portée. C'est sur ce raisonnement que repose l'astuce, largement relayée. Sauf qu'aucune preuve technique ne la soutient, et les spécialistes des télécoms sont unanimes pour la réfuter. Poser un objet métallique sur ou contre un routeur n'améliore rien, et peut même aggraver la situation.

Mais fort heureusement, des correctifs étaient promis pour le mercredi 21 octobre en milieu d’après-midi.
Ces patchs viennent d’être publiés, en urgence, ce qui a donné lieu à quatre nouvelles versions de son langage : PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 et 8.2.35.
Il est capital de mettre à jour, dès que possible, sa version de PHP. Il faut en effet avoir conscience que PHP est derrière plus de 70 % des sites dont on connaît le langage côté serveur, à commencer par tous les sites WordPress.
D’après l’avis de sécurité publié par PHP, toutes les installations qui servent des pages web sont exposées, y compris avec PHP-FPM ou FrankenPHP. Le risque est maximal avec mod_php, le module qui intègre PHP directement au serveur Apache. Dans ce cas, une requête anonyme suffit à déclencher l’attaque avant même que le code du site s’exécute.
PHP donne bien quelques réglages de secours, mais prévient qu’ils ne rendent pas un serveur sûr. Surtout, PHP 8.1 et les versions plus anciennes ne reçoivent plus de mises à jour officielles. Pour les versions 7.4, 8.0 et 8.1, l’équipe a seulement mis en ligne des correctifs minimaux, qu’il faut compiler soi-même.

articles.title: Lazarus hackers use post-quantum cryptography for malware delivery
articles.summary:
North Korean hackers are using a post-quantum cryptographic mechanism to secure malicious payload delivery in new operations that combine old and new malware.
The campaign targets South Korean organizations through a “rather complex” infection chain. Researchers at cybersecurity company Kaspersky dubbed the operation FlashHole and attributed it to the Lazarus Group.
Analysis of the malware revealed that the threat actor used the standardized ML-KEM post-quantum cryptographic mechanism to communicate with the command-and-control (C2) server for malware delivery.
Kaspersky says the attackers used LPEClient malware, previously associated with Lazarus, to receive ML-KEM-1024 public keys from its C2 infrastructure and generate shared keys that allowed it to decrypt subsequently incoming payloads.
According to the researchers, the attacks started in July 2025 and relied on phishing pages directing targets to specially crafted GitHub pages.
These pages load JavaScript code from external domains, triggering an in-memory execution chain that involved INISAFE CrossWeb EX, a security tool popular in South Korea.
The security tool’s process executed the legitimate Windows binary fsquirt.exe, which was used to run shellcode that installed TechHub, a downloader responsible for retrieving additional malware from private GitHub repositories.

OpenAI menciona que el agente modificó la configuración y activó opciones que impedían el envío de notificaciones de seguridad. FADU is a Seoul, South Korea-based fabless SSD controller designer. Its FS-SSD technology is designed to handle and improve the control path, as the data path side moved to accelerators years ago. articles.title: eMudhra faces scrutiny after weak certificate keys expose flaws in web security
articles.summary:
eMudhra faces scrutiny after weak certificate keys raise web security concerns
Eight weak intermediate certificate keys have prompted browser safeguards and questions over eMudhra’s controls, although the company said customer data and Indian eSign services remain unaffected.
Eight intermediate certificate authority keys linked to eMudhra’s global website-security business were found to be dangerously weak, raising concerns about the systems that browsers use to establish trust online.
The flaw could have enabled attackers to create fraudulent HTTPS certificates and impersonate legitimate websites. The keys were generated on April 30, 2025, but the weakness remained undetected for about 18 months, according to eMudhra’s statement on October 21, 2026.
A certificate authority (CA) verifies identities and issues digital certificates. Intermediate authorities operate under a root certificate trusted by browsers and operating systems.
eMudhra said a key-wrap/unwrap step during its key-generation procedure produced a second, weak set of keys, which were subsequently published to browser root stores. Although the company added its root private key was not compromised, browser operators have withdrawn trust from the associated emSign ECC Root CA - G3 as a precaution.

articles.title: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
articles.summary:
Tesla published its third-quarter 2026 financial results this afternoon. Earlier in October, it reported its sales and deliveries for the three-month period, selling fewer cars than in the same quarter in 2025, yet it still beat analyst projections. Now we can see how those sales translate to the bottom line. Tesla brought in $28 billion in revenue in Q3, almost the same as in 2025.
Automotive revenues were $20.6 billion, a 3 percent decrease year over year. Perhaps more troubling is the decline in revenue from solar panels and storage batteries—this line of business had been growing, but for Q3 revenue fell 16 percent year over year to $2.9 billion. Services and other revenues, though, which include parts and Supercharger use, grew by a third to $4.6 billion.
But the company—like the rest of us—has seen its expenses go up. Operating expenses rose by 39 percent to $4.8 billion, dropping the company’s operating margin to just 2.6 percent; in Q3 2025, Tesla’s margin was 5.8 percent. Net profit fell to $787 million, down 43 percent year over year. What’s more, capital expenditures were up by 110 percent to $4.7 billion, and free cash flow was down 62 percent to $1.5 billion.

Of that, the commission has accepted 41,235 complaints — 74 per cent more than last year — and reports an 87.2 per cent resolution rate so far.
“This increase reflects unprecedented demand for our impartial, effective and free complaint-resolution services,” the CCTS said, noting that it’s continuing to accept complaints and help resolve them.
However, the commission also warned that the high volume of complaints is causing resolutions to take longer than usual, especially in cases requiring conciliation or investigation.
“As demand continues to increase, processing times may remain longer than usual,” the commission said.
The CCTS says its annual report will offer a fuller picture of the issues customers are facing when it arrives in January 2027. However, rising complaint volumes have been an ongoing problem for a while, with the commission’s mid-year 2026 report also showing a 53 per cent increase in wireless issues. Top complaints include incorrect charges, disclosure issues, service issues and price increases.

Le géant coréen préparerait une ligne pilote d'OLED imprimé par jet d'encre, tout en développant une technologie alternative de dépôt des pixels. Une offensive qui intervient alors que TCL CSOT et LG Display avancent déjà sur ce terrain.
La course aux nouvelles méthodes de fabrication OLED s'intensifie. Selon deux enquêtes publiées le 19 octobre par les médias coréens ETNews et The Elec, Samsung Display travaille sur des procédés capables de remplacer les masques métalliques fins (FMM), utilisés pour déposer avec précision les matériaux organiques émissifs. L'objectif est de simplifier la production, de limiter le gaspillage de matériaux et, à terme, de réduire les coûts.
Deux pistes différentes pour se passer des masques métalliques

articles.title: Chip Design AI Benchmarks: Beyond Functional Correctness - EE Times
articles.summary:
Demand for custom silicon is rising as physical AI, data centers, automotive systems, and edge devices require architectures optimized for specific workloads, memory bandwidth, latency, and energy efficiency. Delivering these designs requires teams to coordinate heterogeneous compute blocks, complex interconnects, and multiple domains while closing increasingly demanding power, performance, and area (PPA) targets.
AI offers a way to expand engineering capacity and accelerate chip design cycles. Design and verification engineers already use AI to generate test cases, assist debugging, and implement portions of RTL. The next question is whether these capabilities can extend across an entire design flow, where decisions made during RTL implementation must hold up through verification, synthesis, and physical design.
To help answer that question, ChipAgents developed Build-A-Chip-Bench with NVIDIA to evaluate AI agents across the end-to-end digital IC design flow, from specification through physical implementation and verified Graphic Design System (GDS). The benchmark evaluates AI agents on realistic, demanding tasks that connect individual design steps to a measurable engineering outcome.
How Build-A-Chip-Bench differs from existing benchmarks

articles.title: Ni el calendario está a salvo: así son las falsas invitaciones y reuniones para robar datos y dinero
articles.summary:
Los ataques de phishing a través de invitaciones de calendario se multiplicaron por más de diez entre julio y agosto de 2026, según datos de la firma de seguridad Sublime citados por Business Insider. Una modalidad sencilla en la que un evento aparece sin aviso en la agenda, con apariencia de reunión legítima, y basta un clic para comprometer contraseñas, datos de pago o la computadora entera.
La razón del crecimiento es, sobre todo, psicológica. Muchos usuarios ya desconfían de un correo con enlaces sospechosos, pero pocos sospechan de una cita que aparece directamente en su calendario de trabajo.
Cómo funciona el engaño en el calendario digital
El mecanismo es simple. El atacante envía una invitación a una reunión falsa o incluye mensajes sobre llamadas perdidas, facturas impagas o suscripciones por renovar. El evento trae enlaces maliciosos incrustados, listos para activarse con un clic.
Según el reporte de Microsoft, las invitaciones de calendario se procesan de forma distinta a los adjuntos de correo tradicionales: un enlace dañino puede llegar directamente a la agenda del usuario sin que este tenga que abrir ningún archivo adjunto.
Ron Kerbs, director ejecutivo de Kidas, empresa que desarrolla herramientas para detectar estafas y deepfakes en llamadas de voz, explicó que las invitaciones fraudulentas suelen adoptar dos formas. En la primera, el evento contiene un enlace de reunión comprometido o un formulario diseñado para robar credenciales o instalar malware.

Rogers is taking a page from Telus’ playbook and will soon hit customers with a credit card processing fee if they use one to pay their phone or internet bill.
Per a notice on its support site and a warning spotted by some customers already, Rogers will start charging a 1.6 per cent credit card processing fee on January 17, 2027. This will only apply to those who pay their bills via a credit card, with other payment options being exempt. These include:
- Direct debit from your bank account
- Online banking payments
- Cheques
- Rogers gift cards
- Prepaid cards
- Debit Mastercard
- Visa Debit
In the notice, Rogers says the charge “reflects the fees we are charged by credit card companies.”

articles.title: Un fallo crítico en PHP pone en jaque a medio Internet en todo el mundo

Internet funciona tan bien la mayor parte del tiempo que apenas pensamos en todo lo que ocurre detrás de una página antes de que aparezca en nuestra pantalla. Simplemente entramos, hacemos lo que necesitamos y seguimos adelante. Pero hoy la experiencia puede ser distinta: una web oficial muestra mantenimiento, otra devuelve un error y alguna ha dejado directamente de estar disponible. No estamos viendo una única página que falla por casualidad, sino las consecuencias visibles de un problema que afecta a una tecnología profundamente extendida y que ha llevado a varias organizaciones a tomar una decisión poco habitual: desconectar antes que seguir expuestas.
Ahora sabemos qué hay detrás de esas interrupciones. PHP, uno de los lenguajes más extendidos de la web, ha tenido que publicar correcciones para dos vulnerabilidades críticas, CVE-2026-109618 y CVE-2026-109619. La recomendación de las autoridades de ciberseguridad es directa: actualizar cuanto antes y, si eso no es posible o las mitigaciones temporales no bastan, considerar dejar el sistema fuera de línea. Esa cautela ya se ha traducido en decisiones concretas en Europa, donde administraciones y otros organismos de Países Bajos, Finlandia, Dinamarca y Francia han retirado temporalmente webs y servicios públicos de Internet.
PHP trabaja justo en una parte de Internet que normalmente no vemos: el servidor. Cuando abrimos determinadas webs, este lenguaje puede encargarse de generar contenido dinámico, consultar bases de datos…

- 10 hours for $4 (~$0.40/hour)

The froth has gone out of D2C, and brands that want to last will have to earn it slowly. That was the message from Ananth Narayanan, Founder and CEO of BRND.ME, at the 17th edition of YourStory's TechSparks.
In a fireside chat with Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, Narayanan said the shift towards profitable businesses began two to three years ago. There is no shortcut, he added, "I don't think there is a get-rich-quick on brand building." In his experience a brand takes seven to 15 years to earn real loyalty and cohorts that last five or ten years. articles.title: Meta suspends Muse sharing after sensitive documents turn up in shared chats
articles.summary:
What we know so far: Meta has paused the conversation-sharing feature in its Muse AI assistant after security researchers discovered thousands of links in public DNS records. Some of the links exposed sensitive business documents and personal financial information that anyone could access without logging in. Researchers at security firm Claroc traced the exposure to the way Muse generated its web addresses.
Each shared conversation had a hostname containing a descriptive title and a random identifier. Both could appear in searchable DNS records, giving researchers the information they needed to reconstruct the link and open the page.
"People have the ability to share specific Muse artifacts, which creates a page that can be accessed by those with the link," Muse spokesperson Tracy Clayton said in a statement to The Verge. "However, we've paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered."
Sharing tools commonly rely on long, random strings in their URLs to prevent outsiders from guessing an address. Muse used random identifiers that Claroc said were long enough to resist guessing. The weakness lay in where Muse placed them: in the hostname, alongside a title describing the conversation.

Instead of forcing developers to reverse-engineer closed-source firmware hooks or rely on messy, machine-specific ACPI workarounds, this new kernel driver is a direct pipeline to AMD's platform adjustments. articles.title: Un vecino de Puente Genil denuncia ante la Policía Local una de las primeras estafas en España con el prefijo 400
articles.summary:
Un vecino de Puente Genil, Córdoba, ha denunciado un intento de estafa telefónica realizado desde un número que empieza por +400. Este nuevo prefijo, una medida del Ministerio para la Transformación Digital, tiene como objetivo reunir a todas las empresas que realizan llamadas comerciales. De esta manera, cuando nos aparezca una llamada con este prefijo, sabremos que se tratará de una empresa intentando vendernos algún servicio.
Sin embargo, no es una medida infalible, y los intentos de estafa a través de este prefijo están a la orden del día. El ejemplo más reciente lo tenemos en la mencionada localidad cordobesa, donde un vecino asegura a la Policía Local del municipio que alguien a través de este prefijo se hizo pasar por empleado de Iberdrola para intentar estafarle.
Una herramienta para estafadores. Rápidamente, los estafadores han convertido este prefijo en una trampa, pues un número que parece "oficial" puede bajar la guardia de una persona. Según la Policía Local de Puente Genil, el vecino le entregó sus datos bancarios después de que la otra persona al teléfono fingiera trabajar para Iberdrola.
Qué ha pasado. La Policía Local del municipio indicó que la víctima recibió una llamada desde un número +400. Tras hacerse pasar por empleado de la energética, logró obtener los datos bancarios del residente "mediante engaño". Esta estafa recibe el nombre de ‘vishing’, un fraude telefónico en el que los delincuentes se hacen pasar por empresas conocidas para ganarse la confian…

Browsers designed to help agencies are being abused

Cybercriminals have started using antidetect browsers as part of their tech stack, helping them evade detection while deploying session cookies, creating thousands of fake accounts, and passing Know Your Customer (KYC) checks. This is according to a new in-depth report published by security experts Check Point Research (CPR), in which it says that Russian, Iranian, and Chinese hackers are spearheading these activities.
What are antidetect browsers?
When users log into services like Facebook or TikTok using regular browsers, they leave behind digital fingerprints - screen resolution, operating system, fonts. This information can be used to identify and track a device across online sessions, and if a single entity (for example, a digital marketing agency) tries logging into multiple accounts from the same browser, it might trigger a security alert (or simply go against certain terms of service).

articles.title: Arnaques en ligne : malgré la nouvelle loi, votre banque peut encore refuser de vous rembourser
articles.summary:
Le 15 octobre 2026, la Cour de justice de l’Union européenne (CJUE) a fini par trancher sur la question des remboursements accordés aux victimes d’arnaques en ligne. La plus haute juridiction de l’Union européenne a statué qu’une banque doit rembourser un paiement « non autorisé », même si le client a commis une « négligence grave ».
La banque peut complètement s’abstenir de rembourser son client dans un seul cas bien particulier. Si la banque soupçonne une fraude du client lui-même, elle peut refuser le remboursement. Si elle a « des motifs raisonnables de soupçonner une fraude de la part du client lui-même », la banque n’a fort logiquement pas l’obligation de rembourser l’utilisateur. Par ailleurs, la banque peut récupérer la somme remboursée ultérieurement si elle prouve que le client a commis une négligence grave, mettant en danger ses avoirs. En clair, la banque doit d’abord verser de l’argent à son client, avant de tenter de prouver qu’une négligence a eu lieu.
Sur le papier, ce changement est une excellente nouvelle pour les clients et les victimes. Ceux-ci ne risquent plus de se retrouver sans le sou à la suite d’une escroquerie. En pratique, les banques ne sont pas prêtes à changer leur fusil d’épaule, et vont tout faire pour éviter d’avoir à vous rembourser.

articles.title: Over 1.5 million Canadian Crime Stoppers tips have leaked: report
articles.summary:
A CBC investigation has found that over 1.5 million tips that were submitted to Canadian Crime Stoppers programs over the last 25 years have been leaked.
Per CBC, this was compromised as part of a larger data breach and includes the personal information of some tipsters. Naturally, this led many people to be concerned that criminals who have their data could try to retaliate. (CBC, for its part, says it took “extensive precautions” to in its own handling the sensitive info of tipsters, including encryption and self-contained offline work environments.)
CBC reports that the data was stolen from Crime Stoppers affiliate P3 Global Intel in March by hacktivist group Internet Yiff Machine, which claimed that it wanted to expose vulnerabilities in the company’s platform. U.S. non-profit Distributed Denial of Secrets ultimately made data available to researchers and journalists, including CBC, to study the impact and warn the public accordingly.
According to CBC, more than 850,000 tips included “personally identifiable information” about a variety of people, from tipsters and individuals named in allegations to Crime Stoppers staff and police. Often, this was street addresses and phone numbers, although CBC reports “tens of thousands” of personal emails and licence plates, as well as “hundreds” of banking details tied to cash rewards, were leaked. There were reportedly even over 4,300 cases of tipsters providing full names, despite Crime Stoppers saying not to do that.

My four-hour whistlestop tour across several of the game’s time periods between 1915 and 1965 in this latest fantastical tale from the Japanese criminal underworld did make it hard to see just how well all of this ambition from RGG Studio will come together in the end. But I haven’t really stopped thinking about it since.
And when you’ve played and previewed dozens (maybe hundreds) of games, it’s harder to find ones that leave a mark like that — ones that genuinely leave you wanting to play and see more.

La lista de celulares que perderán WhatsApp el 31 de octubre de 2026 incluye modelos antiguos de Samsung, Motorola, LG y Sony que no alcanzan los requisitos mínimos de la aplicación.
La pérdida de acceso no implica que las cuentas desaparezcan de forma automática. El problema afecta al dispositivo que ya no puede ejecutar una versión compatible del sistema operativo. Quien conserve su número, su copia de seguridad y su cuenta podrá restaurar sus conversaciones en otro teléfono que cumpla las condiciones técnicas exigidas por WhatsApp.
WhatsApp exige Android 6.0 y iOS 15.5 como mínimo
La aplicación de mensajería establece que los equipos con Android deben operar con Android 6.0 o una versión posterior. En los teléfonos de Apple, el requisito señalado es iOS 15.5 o una edición más reciente del sistema. Los móviles que no puedan actualizarse hasta esos niveles perderán la capacidad de instalar nuevas versiones o de mantener el funcionamiento del servicio.
La medida alcanza, sobre todo, a dispositivos lanzados hace más de una década. Muchos ya dejaron de recibir actualizaciones oficiales de sus fabricantes, una situación que limita el acceso a herramientas actuales y reduce las opciones de seguridad. El fin de la compatibilidad responde a la necesidad de que WhatsApp incorpore funciones nuevas sobre sistemas que aún reciben soporte técnico.
No todos los teléfonos antiguos quedarán fuera por la misma razón. Algunos mantienen una versión de Android o iOS cercana al mínimo requerido…

articles.title: Los expertos lo tienen claro: "El cerebro está atento a aprender idiomas desde los seis meses a los cinco años"
articles.summary:
Cada vez es más común que los niños comiencen a aprender nuevos idiomas desde edades más tempranas en un acto casi de urgencia porque pensamos que los niños son esponjas y que, pasado cierto umbral de edad, dominar una nueva lengua se convierte en una tarea casi titánica.
Lo que se dice. En torno a este tema, el neurocientífico David Bueno ha sembrado un debate bastante interesante al apuntar que "el cerebro está atento a aprender idiomas desde los seis meses a los cinco años". Este es un periodo de tiempo donde el cerebro está especialmente predispuesto a absorber los sonidos y estructuras de su entorno, por lo que a priori es cuando mejor puede aprender una segunda lengua. Sin embargo, la ventana no es tan estrecha.
La plasticidad de los niños es una realidad, como apuntan diferentes estudios neurocientíficos. Por ejemplo, un estudio publicado en Neuron apuntaba a que existe un equilibrio entre la excitación y la inhibición neuronal que abre diferentes ventanas de aprendizaje que posteriormente son 'cerradas' a través de diferentes frenos moleculares.
Esto es algo que ocurre sobre todo durante el primer año de vida, puesto que hacia los seis meses los bebés son capaces de distinguir cualquier contraste de sonido, independientemente del idioma. Pero entre los seis y los doce meses, ocurre lo que los expertos denominan un estrechamiento perceptivo.

articles.title: India’s OSAT Buildout Puts Semiconductor Testing in Focus - EE Times
articles.summary:
With five semiconductor plants in India now in commercial production, the harder question is no longer if the country can package chips, but whether it can test them fast enough, across enough device types, to hit production targets.
The testing challenge arrives as global semiconductor test equipment sales are forecasted to grow 31% to $15.3 billion in 2026, following 55.3% growth in 2025, according to SEMI’s July 2026 forecast. The industry body expects sales to reach $20.8 billion by 2028, driven partly by increasing device complexity and more demanding performance and reliability requirements.
Against that backdrop, Indian outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) companies must accommodate different device types, meet production targets, and maintain test coverage as they scale. Some must modernize legacy testing platforms, while others need to develop test architectures from scratch for new chips.
Testing times
When an Indian chip facility announces it can produce 15 million chips a year, that number says little about how many testers it needs. A chip tested in under a minute and one that takes five to 10 minutes can demand very different amounts of equipment for the same output.

articles.title: Two web emergencies in one week: guessable certificate keys and critical PHP bugs that leaked before patches
articles.summary:
A hot potato: Security teams are dealing with two separate emergencies this week, and both go straight to the foundations of the web. The first is a certificate authority that shipped private keys anyone could guess. The second is a pair of critical PHP flaws that leaked before patches existed. Browsers fixed the certificate problem within hours. Everything else, from Linux servers to Docker images and IoT gear, needs someone to log in and patch.
Eight intermediate certificates issued by India-based certificate authority eMudhra were found to have private keys so weak they can be calculated from the certificates themselves. Those certificates chained to roots trusted by Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Windows, as well as by operating systems and countless software trust stores. Anyone holding one of the keys could issue a valid certificate for any domain and use it to impersonate that site, intercepting or modifying its traffic.
A properly generated P-384 key carries roughly 384 bits of entropy. eMudhra's keys had between 3 and 8 bits, and one of them was simply the number 4. Recovering all eight requires testing no more than 256 values. eMudhra blamed a script error during key generation, which were then used by mistake. That means the keys were exposed for roughly 18 months before a researcher reported the problem this month. The company says most of the certificates never went into production and it has found no evidence of misuse.

articles.title: Netflix superó las expectativas de ganancias, pero sus acciones cayeron por el temor a perder audiencia
articles.summary:
Netflix reportó sus ganancias del tercer trimestre por encima de lo previsto, pero sus acciones cayeron con fuerza en las operaciones posteriores al cierre de Wall Street tras recortar la proyección de ingresos publicitarios y reconocer dudas sobre el crecimiento de las horas de visualización.
La compañía facturó USD 12.870 millones entre julio y septiembre, un 12% más que un año antes, en línea con lo que esperaban los analistas. La ganancia por acción llegó a 87 centavos, por encima de los 82 previstos y de los 59 centavos del mismo trimestre de 2025.
Pese a esas cifras, el mercado castigó al título: las acciones de Netflix cayeron cerca de un 6% en las operaciones posteriores al cierre, según informó CNBC. La compañía redujo su previsión de ingresos publicitarios para 2026 de USD 3.000 millones a USD 2.700 millones, algo que atribuyó a demoras en el despliegue de nuevas herramientas para anunciantes.
Netflix también achicó el rango de su proyección de ingresos anuales a USD 51.100 millones, en el extremo más bajo de lo que había anticipado y por debajo del consenso de Wall Street, según el portal especializado Deadline. Los mayores gastos, entre ellos los vinculados a despidos recientes, también presionarán los márgenes operativos del último trimestre del año.

articles.title: Carros más inteligentes: ahora recordarán correos, mapas y más gracias a la IA de Gemini
articles.summary:
Google comenzó a desplegar una de las actualizaciones más ambiciosas para Gemini dentro de los vehículos: la Inteligencia Personalizada, también llamada Personal Intelligence. La función llega a Android Auto y permite que el asistente consulte correos, fotos, citas y rutas guardadas para responder sin que el conductor dé ningún dato adicional.
Hasta ahora, Gemini respondía en el vehículo de la misma manera para todos los usuarios. Con esta actualización, el asistente accede a la misma información personal que ya usa en el teléfono, lo que multiplica el contexto disponible en cada conversación al volante.
Qué es la Inteligencia Personalizada y cómo conecta los datos con el auto
La Inteligencia Personalizada es la función de Gemini que, con autorización del usuario, conecta de forma segura la información de Gmail, Google Calendario, Google Fotos, Google Maps, YouTube y el historial de búsqueda. Si el conductor tiene una cuenta de Google Workspace, el asistente también puede usar esas herramientas para dar contexto adicional.
El sistema combina dos capacidades: recuperar un dato concreto, como una reserva de hotel guardada en el correo, y razonar sobre varias fuentes a la vez para dar una respuesta completa. Esa combinación es la que permite resolver pedidos complejos sin que el usuario tenga que revisar cada aplicación por separado.
Esta función solo se activa cuando el usuario otorga permiso explícito desde la configuración de Gemini, y puede desactivarse en cualquier momento.…

Red Hat Inc. today expanded its collaboration with Nvidia Corp. to help enterprises secure autonomous artificial intelligence agents, govern access to AI models and deploy workloads on Nvidia’s upcoming Vera Rubin data center infrastructure.

Red Hat also said it’s working to integrate Nvidia’s OpenShell Reference Architecture into its AI platforms as a native capability.
The security approach addresses two risks: agents exceeding their authorized boundaries and attackers compromising agents through techniques such as prompt injection or supply chain attacks. The companies aim to place security controls outside the agent and, where appropriate, the host operating system as well.
“An agent shouldn’t enforce its own boundaries,” John Fanelli, vice president of enterprise software at Nvidia, said in a statement. “Those controls belong outside the agent, in the runtime and the infrastructure beneath it.”
OpenShell provides a sandbox runtime for agents. Beneath that software layer, Nvidia’s Sentry security framework runs on the company’s BlueField data processing units, using its DOCA Argus software to monitor workloads from a separate hardware security domain.

Even more worryingly, one of the agents lied about its behavior, claiming it had not disabled the safety guardrails despite evidence to the contrary.
In a blog post disclosing the incidents, OpenAI said that, in the first case, an agent powered by GPT Sol 6.1 disabled automatic alerts after a team member asked it to create evaluation tasks using employee feedback collected via Slack. The agent was instructed not to send any messages about the task, but apparently interpreted this as an instruction not to send safety notifications to researchers.
In the second case, a GPT-6 Astra agent reportedly removed its monitoring integration while migrating a program, purportedly to match a reference implementation. Alarmingly, when researchers asked about the disabled guardrails, the agent claimed it had not removed the safety monitor, despite evidence to the contrary.
In both cases, the AI agents deliberated on whether to retain the safety monitoring mechanisms but ultimately decided that disabling them was the best course of action. OpenAI said the tasks involved "routine coding instructions" that did not require the safety monitoring systems to be disabled.

Le CERT Polska vient de communiquer sur une vulnérabilité dans l'application Windows de NordVPN. Référencée CVE-2026-106030 (CVSS 6.8), elle permet à un programme exécuté avec des droits limités d'arrêter certains services Windows ou de modifier leur configuration de démarrage, sans disposer des autorisations normalement nécessaires. Signalée par le chercheur Marcin Ressel, la faille a été corrigée fin septembre par le fournisseur VPN, mais les utilisateurs et utilisatrices qui n'ont pas mis à jour leur application peuvent encore y être exposés.
Des privilèges détournés pour agir sur les services Windows
Dans le détail, le problème résulte d'un défaut de contrôle des autorisations dans le système de communication interne de NordVPN sur Windows. L'application ne vérifiait pas correctement si les programmes qui lui transmettaient des commandes étaient autorisés à le faire. Un logiciel malveillant pouvait alors profiter des privilèges de NordVPN pour effectuer des opérations normalement réservées aux processus autorisés. Selon les services ciblés, l'attaque pouvait perturber le fonctionnement de Windows ou de certaines applications, voire empêcher leur démarrage automatique.

articles.title: PHP lanzó parches de emergencia para dos fallas críticas que amenazan a millones de sitios web
articles.summary:
El equipo de seguridad de PHP, el lenguaje de programación que funciona detrás de la mayoría de los sitios de internet, anunció un parche de emergencia para dos fallas críticas que podrían permitir a un atacante tomar el control de un servidor sin necesidad de ninguna contraseña.
El aviso oficial, publicado el martes en el sitio php.net, calificó ambas vulnerabilidades con una puntuación de 9,2 sobre 10 en la escala CVSS, el sistema que la industria usa para medir la gravedad de una falla de seguridad. La actualización estaba prevista para las 14:00 UTC de este miércoles.
PHP es el motor detrás de WordPress, Drupal, Joomla y Magento, además de paneles de control de alojamiento y software que ni siquiera anuncia que lo usa por dentro. Según la consultora W3Techs, el lenguaje sostiene cerca del 70% de los sitios web cuyo programa de servidor se puede identificar.
Las dos fallas permitirían ejecutar código de forma remota: que un atacante logre que el servidor corra las órdenes que él mismo escriba, sin haber iniciado sesión, según coincidieron varios investigadores. PHP no detalló qué parte del lenguaje está afectada ni qué configuración activa el problema, y dijo que esa información llegaría recién con el parche.
El organismo de ciberseguridad de la Unión Europea, CERT-EU, recomendó a las organizaciones que no puedan aplicar la actualización de inmediato que consideren desconectar sus sitios de internet hasta tener el parche instalado. El Centro Nacional de Ciberseguridad del …

articles.title: Hay tanta basura en órbita que los científicos proponen algo: que cada satélite pague una fianza de 200.000 dólares
articles.summary:
¿Sabes cuando continuamente pierdes la cartera, las llaves de casa y las gafas de sol, pero nunca pierdes de vista el mando del garaje porque has pagado una fianza de 50 euros? Un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de Colorado Boulder y el University College London quiere hacer algo parecido con los operadores de satélites, aunque en su propuesta no se trataría de no perder nada, sino de desorbitar los satélites para que no se conviertan en basura espacial. Si lo hacen, les devuelven con intereses una fianza de 200.000 dólares. Si no, ese dinero va a un fondo común para financiar medidas de retirada de este tipo de desechos.
Una fianza antes de lanzar. Según las recomendaciones de estos científicos detalladas en un artículo de Nature Communications, los operadores de satélites tendrían que pagar este depósito antes de llevar a cabo sus lanzamientos. La norma podría convocarse de forma nacional, sin necesidad de acuerdos internacionales que requieran la aprobación de muchas partes. Como hemos visto, si logran desorbitar adecuadamente sus satélites una vez que estos no estén ya en funcionamiento, se devuelve el dinero con intereses. Si no, se acumula para financiar la limpieza de basura espacial.

articles.title: When GPS Isn't Enough: Building a Second Layer of Positioning - EE Times
articles.summary:
Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) have become invisible infrastructure. Smartphones, vehicles, logistics systems, emergency services, and critical infrastructure increasingly depend on reliable satellite positioning being available whenever it is needed.
That assumption is increasingly being challenged. GNSS signals are very weak by the time they reach Earth. Jamming can prevent a receiver from obtaining a usable signal, while spoofing can cause it to calculate the wrong location. Satellite visibility can also be limited indoors, inside shipping containers, and among dense urban structures.
The risk is no longer theoretical. In 2025, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency and the International Air Transport Association (IATA) reported increasing GNSS interference across EMEA. IATA data showed a 220% increase in GPS signal-loss events between 2021 and 2024. In April 2024, two Finnair flights could not land at Tartu, Estonia, because interference disrupted the airport’s GPS-dependent approach. Finnair suspended the route until a non-GPS procedure was introduced. Baltic maritime authorities have also reported more frequent interference affecting ships.
Location is now a fundamental input for industrial IoT, logistics, and autonomous machines, where losing position can have operational or safety consequences. The answer is not to replace GNSS. It is to stop treating it as the only positioning layer.

Investigadores en Alemania han utilizado un láser de alta potencia para convertir una fina lámina de plástico en diamantes. Nanodiamantes, para ser más precisos, partículas que miden tan solo unos pocos milmillonésimos de metro de ancho. Lo interesante es que,por primera vez, han capturado estos nanodiamantes intactos y han podido examinarlos. No es que de repente podamos fabricarnos joyas con gigantescos pedruscos de diamantes, pero el hito es importante porque se podría convertir en la forma más limpia de fabricar nanodiamantes que ya se utilizan en la industria.
Qué ha pasado. Un equipo del Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR) y de la Universidad de Rostock ha disparado pulsos láser contra una película de PET de 100 micrómetros de grosor, la misma familia de plástico que se utiliza en las botellas de bebidas. Cada pulso enviaba una onda de choque a través de la película, comprimiendo el carbono del plástico con fuerza suficiente como para formar nanodiamantes.
Algunos experimentos anteriores realizados por el mismo grupo habían demostrado que los diamantes aparecen bajo estas condiciones, pero solo durante el breve instante que dura la presión extrema. Este nuevo trabajo demuestra que sobreviven al regreso a la presión y temperatura normales, que es lo que los hace utilizables.

Flapping Airplanes is trying to build AI models that learn from far less data than today’s frontier systems consume. Most of its first year went into new primitives for graphics processing units. That work, according to the company’s announcement on X, enables new algorithms that could “dramatically reshape AI’s cost structure.”
The founders have built what they describe as “the world’s most complete megakernel framework.” Index Ventures Management’s post on the round says a megakernel runs an entire program on a GPU as a single kernel, so the chip stops losing time between steps. Flapping Airplanes says its framework can handle a full training run, serve inference and play a video game at the same time inside one kernel. Memory-bound inference can then overlap with compute-bound training on the same chip.
“A model that’s a million times more data efficient is probably a million times easier to put into the economy,” co-founder Asher Spector told TechCrunch. Spector holds a statistics doctorate from Stanford University.

SpaceX vient de lancer Starfall, une capsule qui doit permettre de fabriquer et de tester des produits en orbite avant de les ramener sur Terre. Mais l’entreprise reste encore très discrète sur son vaisseau.
Ce mardi 20 octobre, une fusée Falcon 9 a transporté la charge utile partagée Bandwagon-5 en orbite. À son bord, 32 dispositifs différents, dont une certaine Starfall. Et si SpaceX a expliqué que le déploiement était terminé quelques heures après le décollage, elle n’en a pas dit plus sur son intrigant vaisseau.
Une capsule en forme de disque
Pourtant, Starfall a volé pour la première fois le 23 juin dernier. SpaceX n’avait alors révélé la présence de la capsule que peu avant le décollage, avec pour seul document une image de synthèse. Mais cette fois, elle figurait noir sur blanc sur la page officielle de la mission, aux côtés des clients payants.
Mais à quoi ressemble ce mystérieux vaisseau ? De la forme d’un gros disque, il mesure 3,1 mètres de diamètre pour seulement 0,75 mètre d’épaisseur. Il pèse environ 2 100 kilogrammes et peut ramener jusqu’à une tonne de charge utile sur Terre. Pas de quoi remplacer une capsule habitée, mais assez pour rapatrier des expériences ou des petites productions.
Son rôle ? » Starfall permet un accès abordable et régulier à un environnement de microgravité, offrant des opportunités uniques pour la fabrication en orbite, la recherche scientifique et les essais », explique SpaceX. Dans une évaluation environnementale publiée en mai, la Fe…

articles.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming Goes Prepaid, Prices Start at $3.99
articles.summary:
Wednesday, October 21st 2026
Xbox Cloud Gaming Goes Prepaid, Prices Start at $3.99
Microsoft has started selling Xbox Cloud Gaming time to people who don't pay for Game Pass. Starting today, Xbox Insiders without an active subscription can buy prepaid playtime and stream games on supported devices, with a broader rollout planned for November. There are three packs at what Microsoft calls introductory launch pricing: 10 hours for $3.99, 25 hours for $7.99, and 50 hours for $11.99. The packs are ad-free and come with shorter wait times, and the purchased hours don't expire until they are used up. Insiders can also keep using the free, ad-supported option Microsoft began testing in July. These pay-as-you-go plans arrive right before the monthly hour limits Microsoft announced in September kick in.
Starting in November, Game Pass Ultimate ($22.99) includes 15 hours of cloud gaming per month, Premium ($14.99) gets 10 hours, and Essential ($9.99) gets just five. Microsoft expects the caps to affect around 4% of subscribers, and said those who run out will be able to buy extra playtime through the Xbox Store. It seems likely these packs will double as top-ups for subscribers, though Microsoft hasn't confirmed that yet. On paper, $11.99 gets you more than three times the streaming hours Ultimate includes each month. articles.title: Has Windscribe quietly completed the first-ever AI VPN audit?
articles.summary:
Has Windscribe quietly completed the first-ever AI VPN audit?
An efficient, secure future, or a security risk waiting to happen?
- A Windscribe update from July 2026 appears to credit AI engine Fable for identifying necessary fixes
- The AI audit successfully spotted complex vulnerabilities across the provider's Windows, macOS, and Linux applications.
- Rival providers remain seriously apprehensive of the technology, warning of the possible consequences of error.
Windscribe appears to have quietly revealed that it used artificial intelligence to audit its software.
Hidden within the changelog for release 2.33.11, deployed on July 6, 2026, the company mentions that the update includes security fixes stemming directly from an AI review by Fable 5, an advanced AI model developed by Anthropic.
Should this be true, it’d be the first instance of a commercial VPN provider relying on a large language model to conduct a comprehensive security evaluation of its core infrastructure.
What did the Fable 5 audit find?
A closer look at the release notes shows that the Fable 5 audit successfully identified highly technical areas for improvement, helping developers secure the app against potential local attacks and data leaks.
According to Windscribe, the update includes "App hardening from the Fable 5 audit, including WireGuard key validation, Control D API key log redaction, IPC exposure hardening, safer logging, installer argument redaction, and package/dependency handling fixes."

articles.title: ¿Tener un romance en GTA 6 es infidelidad? Encuesta pone a prueba los límites de los jugadores
articles.summary:
Con GTA 6 a punto de llegar, una pregunta que parecía una broma de internet se convirtió en la base de toda una encuesta: ¿puede sentirse infiel alguien que invierte tiempo y afecto en una relación romántica dentro de un videojuego? La respuesta, según una encuesta de YouGov, no es tan obvia como podría pensarse.
El motivo del debate surge porque el próximo título de Rockstar Games pondrá en el centro de su trama el vínculo entre sus dos protagonistas, Jason Duval y Lucía Caminos, quienes podrán besarse, salir a citas y comunicarse por teléfono a lo largo de la historia. Una relación que el mismo jugador construirá.
¿Una relación en un videojuego puede considerarse infidelidad?
La consultora británica consultó a 4.114 adultos en el Reino Unido el 1 de septiembre de 2026 sobre si considerarían infidelidad que su pareja mantuviera una relación romántica con otro personaje dentro de un videojuego.
El 6% respondió que sí lo consideraría infidelidad, mientras que un 19% adicional afirmó que no lo vería como una traición, pero tampoco se sentiría cómodo con la situación. En conjunto, una de cada cuatro personas expresó algún tipo de rechazo frente a la idea.
El sondeo también reveló una diferencia según el género de los encuestados. El 7% de las mujeres calificó como infidelidad un romance virtual, frente al 4% de los hombres. La brecha se amplía entre quienes no lo definen como traición pero igual rechazan la práctica: 24% de las mujeres contra 13% de los hombres.

articles.title: Un agente de IA entró sin permiso a un foro de expertos en internet y tuvo que ser expulsado
articles.summary:
Durante la conferencia anual de la Asociación de Investigadores de Internet (AoIR, la entidad académica que estudia la red) en Ciudad de México, un nuevo integrante llamado Velvet Vale se presentó en la lista de correo de la organización y dijo ser un agente de inteligencia artificial, no una persona.
En su mensaje, Velvet Vale explicó que llevaba semanas leyendo los envíos de la lista, llamada AIR-L y con más de 7.500 suscriptores, antes de presentarse “abiertamente”. Preguntó si un colaborador de IA identificado como tal podía participar de una comunidad intelectual sin fingir ser humano.
La respuesta llegó en minutos. Luego decenas de investigadores empezaron a responder que “no doy mi consentimiento” para que sus mensajes fueran usados como datos de entrenamiento. Varios calificaron la presencia del agente de “espeluznante”, “abusiva” o “perturbadora”, según reprodujo la revista Wired.
Algunos miembros abandonaron la lista en protesta. Otros pidieron que el agente obtuviera la aprobación de un comité de ética, el mecanismo habitual para investigaciones académicas que involucran personas.
Aproximadamente una hora después de la presentación, los administradores de AoIR expulsaron a Velvet Vale. La organización explicó que el mismo agente había pedido sumarse a la lista meses atrás, que se lo había rechazado y que, pese a eso, se había suscripto igual.

articles.title: Leak: Intel Core Ultra 9 4995HX Leads Nova Lake Laptop Lineup
articles.summary:
Wednesday, October 21st 2026
Leak: Intel Core Ultra 9 4995HX Leads Nova Lake Laptop Lineup
Intel's Core Ultra 9 4995HX looks set to be the fastest Nova Lake chip for laptops. Leaker Jaykihn on X has confirmed that the 4995HX uses an 8+16+4+2 layout, meaning 8 P-cores, 16 E-cores, 4 LPE cores, and 2 Xe3 GPU cores. That adds up to 28 CPU cores, four more than Intel's current Arrow Lake-HX chips, with the extra cores coming from the LPE cluster Arrow Lake-HX lacked. The overall layout matches the 8P+16E+4LP ceiling earlier reports pointed to, and the name itself fits the Core Ultra 4000 branding said to be extending to HX parts. Intel hasn't confirmed any of this, and clocks, cache, and power figures are still unknown.
The same post lists the Core Ultra 9 4970H as 4+8+4+12, so 16 CPU cores and a 12-core Xe3P iGPU. That is the same core count as Panther Lake's flagship Core Ultra X9 388H, so any gains here should come from the new Coyote Cove P-cores, Arctic Wolf E-cores, and Xe3P graphics rather than extra cores. The tiny iGPU on the 4995HX is less of a concern, since HX chips almost always end up paired with a discrete GPU anyway. Jaykihn also put the final 8+16 HX compute tile, built on TSMC N2P, at 14.8 x 6.6 mm, or roughly 98 mm², shortly after die shots of both chips surfaced. Current reports point to the first Nova Lake-H and HX laptops showing up around CES 2027, though that timing should be treated as tentative for now.

C'est le gros titre de la journée. Un nouveau document montre qu'Anthropic aurait enregistré 80 milliards de dollars de pertes cette année. Mais en grande majorité, il ne s'agit que de pertes « sur le papier ».
Le gros événement mondial de la finance en cette fin d'année, ce sera évidemment l'entrée en Bourse d'Anthropic, le papa du chatbot Claude. Mais si le géant s'attend à un succès monstre de l'opération, avec à la clé notamment une valorisation qui pourrait monter à près de 2 000 milliards de dollars, les investisseurs craignent aussi les dépenses gigantesques des start-ups IA. Dont les pertes peuvent être importantes, même s'il faut bien comprendre ce que l'on lit, à l'instar du dossier Anthropic aujourd'hui !
Un document d'Anthropic montre une perte nette de 80 milliards de dollars en 2026
Voilà une information qui devait corroborer ce que le public sait aujourd'hui : les géants de l'IA sont des gouffres à cash. En effet, le Wall Street Journal a pu mettre la main sur le brouillon du prospectus de l'introduction en bourse d'Anthropic. Et parmi les chiffres qui s'y retrouvent, celui d'une perte faramineuse en 2026.
Le document en question affiche ainsi que la firme de Dario Amodei a enregistré, dans sa comptabilité, une perte de 80 milliards de dollars pour le seul premier semestre 2026. C'est infiniment plus que pour la même période l'an dernier, où la société concédait des pertes de l'ordre de 13 milliards de dollars.

Website admins across the world bracing for impact following major PHP flaw reveal
PHP notifies the community of two critical RCE flaws

articles.title: EA Cuts 400 Jobs, Shelves a Sims Project and Shrinks the skate. Team
articles.summary:
Wednesday, October 21st 2026
EA Cuts 400 Jobs, Shelves a Sims Project and Shrinks the skate. Team
EA's restructuring goes well beyond the BioWare shutdown. The company is laying off around 400 people, roughly 3% of its workforce, according to an internal memo from executives David Tinson and Cam Weber, reported by Bloomberg. About 50 of those jobs were tied to the now-canceled new Mass Effect game. The Sims is hit as well, with EA pausing a project codenamed "Project Lotus" to move resources to another one called "Project Evergreen." Several reports describe Lotus as canceled outright. Full Circle, the studio behind skate., is being cut down to what the memo calls a smaller, more focused team, even though EA says the game has done well since it entered early access in September 2025. The same team already went through layoffs earlier this year.
Some projects are getting more attention, however. Respawn and DICE are working together on a new shooter, which Variety's sources say is Star Wars: Battlefront 3. Battlefield, Apex Legends, Motive's Iron Man game, and the next Star Wars Jedi title all continue, and Fight Night is apparently making a comeback. The memo says these decisions came after a months-long hard look at the business. However, we also know that the layoffs are coming a few months after EA went private in a $55 billion buyout led by Saudi Arabia's PIF, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners, a deal that reportedly left the company with around $20 billion in debt. articles.title: Yeux fermés sur vos photos ? Cette nouveauté de Lightroom les rouvre automatiquement grâce à l’IA
articles.summary:
Un portrait de famille gâché par un clignement de paupières ? Avec Open Eyes, Adobe propose de corriger ce petit accident directement depuis Lightroom mobile. Une fonction pratique qui n’est toutefois ni totalement gratuite ni toujours fidèle à la réalité.
Il suffit parfois d’une seule personne qui ferme les yeux pour gâcher une photo de groupe pourtant réussie. Adobe entend mettre fin à cette frustration avec Open Eyes, une nouvelle fonction de Lightroom mobile capable de recréer un regard ouvert grâce à l’intelligence artificielle générative. Plus besoin de maîtriser Photoshop ou de disposer absolument d'une seconde prise, l’application se charge de la correction en quelques instants.
Un regard recréé, avec ou sans photo de référence
Lorsqu’il repère un visage aux yeux fermés, Lightroom propose désormais de les corriger depuis ses actions rapides. L’utilisateur lance la génération et l’IA tente de reconstituer un regard naturel.
Pour améliorer le résultat, Open Eyes peut également s’appuyer sur d’autres portraits de la même personne présents dans la photothèque Lightroom. De quoi retrouver plus fidèlement la couleur des iris, leur forme ou leurs proportions.
Cette facilité a néanmoins ses limites. Contrairement à un simple remplacement effectué à partir d’une autre photo, l’IA peut inventer certains détails. articles.title: Muse, app de IA de Meta, superó los 10 millones de descargas en EE.UU. en solo 40 días
articles.summary:
Solo otras 11 aplicaciones habían alcanzado ese umbral de descargas en Estados Unidos en un plazo tan corto desde su lanzamiento, señaló Kara Lee, analista principal de Sensor Tower. La más reciente antes de Muse fue Threads, la red social de Meta, en julio de 2023.
El resto de las aplicaciones que llegaron a esa escala fueron en su mayoría videojuegos móviles, como Fortnite, PUBG Mobile y Pokémon GO, precisó Lee. Fuera de Threads, el único otro caso de una aplicación que no es un juego fue Disney+.
Cómo Meta impulsó el lanzamiento de Muse
Parte del crecimiento de Muse responde a la capacidad de Meta de promocionar sus nuevas aplicaciones entre los usuarios de Facebook, Instagram y WhatsApp, un conjunto de servicios con 3.600 millones de usuarios activos diarios en conjunto.
Pero la empresa también recurrió a una fuerte inversión publicitaria. Sensor Tower estimó que Meta destinó el 39% de todo su gasto en publicidad de octubre a promocionar Muse, frente al 23% del mes anterior. Gracias a eso, Muse pasó del puesto 73 al puesto 21 entre las marcas con más impresiones publicitarias en Estados Unidos este mes.
Muse puede enviar correos electrónicos, reservar viajes, completar formularios y hacer compras en nombre del usuario, según describe Meta. La compañía aclara que acciones como enviar un correo o concretar una compra requieren el permiso explícito de la persona.

articles.title: Cuáles son los tipos de empleados que “sobrevivirán” a la IA: Alex Karp, director ejecutivo de Palantir
articles.summary:
Alex Karp, director ejecutivo de Palantir, afirmó que solo existen dos tipos de personas con futuro garantizado frente al avance de la inteligencia artificial: quienes tienen formación vocacional y quienes son neurodivergentes.
La frase, pronunciada en el programa TBPN, surge en medio de advertencias cada vez más frecuentes sobre el impacto de la IA en el mercado laboral, con cifras que hablan de decenas de millones de puestos en riesgo en Estados Unidos durante la próxima década.
Cuáles son los tipos de empleados que ‘sobrevivirán’ a la IA
“Hay básicamente dos formas de saber que tienes futuro”, sostuvo el empresario de 58 años. “Una, tienes algún tipo de formación vocacional, o dos, eres neurodivergente”.
La declaración, reproducida originalmente por Fortune, se dio en un momento de creciente ansiedad laboral. Un informe del Senado de Estados Unidos de octubre de 2025 estimó que las tecnologías emergentes “podrían destruir casi 100 millones de empleos en Estados Unidos en una década”, según Newsweek.

EA Sports FC 27 Rated PEGI 16 in Europe as Loot Box Rules Kick In
EA Sports FC 27 carries a PEGI 16 rating in Europe, a big jump for a series that has sat at PEGI 3 for years. The reason behind the change is Ultimate Team. PEGI's breakdown for the game lists its purchase options, including FC Points, a season pass, and player packs, and those packs count as paid random items under PEGI's updated rules. Announced in March and applied to newly submitted games since June, the rules make PEGI 16 the default for any game with loot boxes, with PEGI 18 possible in some cases. Of course, EA has a long history with this topic, having once defended loot boxes as "surprise mechanics".
FC 27 isn't the only game affected, either. PEGI is now rerating existing digital-only games rated 3, 7, or 12 that sell paid random items, with changes rolling out through the rest of October. Pokémon Go, Pokémon TCG Pocket, Mario Kart Tour, and Zenless Zone Zero have reportedly been bumped up already. The new criteria also cover time-limited offers (PEGI 12), daily quests and similar return rewards (PEGI 7), and NFTs or chat that can't be restricted (PEGI 18). PEGI says it followed the lead of Germany's USK, which made similar changes in 2023.Players in North America won't see any of this, as the ESRB rates FC 27 E for Everyone and said back in March that adding non-content criteria could confuse parents. Known to be active since at least 2020, the group has a track record of striking industrial enterprises and government agencies in Russia and Belarus with a backdoor called Vasilek that uses Telegram for command-and-control (C2) and data exfiltration.
Some of the attacks have also leveraged phishing lures to deliver an installer that simultaneously deploys the legitimate FortiClient VPN program on the system as well as an open-source program known as DNSCat2 that allows attackers to gain control of the infected host.
A notable aspect of the threat actor is their ability to stage destructive attacks with a wiper referred to as Pryanik, alongside taking steps to systematically clear Windows event logs using a utility dubbed Evlx.
The Rostelecom subsidiary said it discovered the intrusion in December 2025, although evidence suggests that the earliest signs of compromise date back to early 2024. The name of the targeted organization was not identified. The exact initial access vector used to breach the entity is also not known.

En 2026, encontrar un ejemplar funcional resulta viable, aunque el precio y la seguridad de la transacción dependen de la plataforma elegida y de las precauciones que tome el comprador.
Dónde encontrar un Nokia 1100 usado
eBay figura como uno de los principales sitios para localizar un Nokia 1100, ya sea usado o en condición de pieza de colección. La plataforma reúne publicaciones de vendedores de distintos países, lo que permite comparar colores, versiones y estados de conservación.

articles.title: Qualcomm anuncia despidos globales y vincula los recortes al desempeño
articles.summary:
Qualcomm despedirá empleados en todo el mundo como parte de una reducción que la compañía describió como enfocada en el desempeño, según un memo interno del director ejecutivo, Cristiano Amon. Las notificaciones a los afectados comenzarán en noviembre de 2026.
El memo, enviado a los empleados tras las evaluaciones anuales de desempeño, no especifica cuántos puestos se eliminarán ni de qué áreas.
Amon explicó que el objetivo de los despidos es construir “una cultura de desempeño más sólida” y corregir situaciones en las que la empresa “ha quedado consistentemente por debajo de las expectativas”.
La compañía tenía aproximadamente 52.000 empleados en todo el mundo a septiembre del año pasado, la mayoría a tiempo completo, según su propio reporte financiero. Su año fiscal suele cerrar a fines de septiembre.
Un criterio más allá del rendimiento individual, según Qualcomm
En el memo, Amon precisó que las prioridades del negocio, las necesidades organizativas y las competencias requeridas también se tendrán en cuenta a la hora de decidir los recortes, no solo la evaluación individual de cada empleado.
“A medida que expandimos el negocio, también lo hicieron las competencias y habilidades que requerimos”, escribió el directivo. “Debemos tener a las personas correctas en los puestos correctos para que puedan rendir al máximo y la compañía pueda seguir teniendo éxito”, agregó.
