articles.title: State Bank of India Confirms Data Leak After 3,897 Customer Records Found on Dark Web
articles.summary:
State Bank of India has identified 3,897 customer records containing personal information in a set of about 375,000 records available on the dark web, and it does not yet know where the data came from.
The state-owned bank, India's largest, said in a stock-exchange filing dated October 21 that it "has experienced an incident involving the loss of certain data." The count is preliminary, and the bank has yet to establish whether the data is authentic, how far the exposure goes and what risk it poses to customers.
The exposed information "reportedly included customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files," in the filing's words. A CIF identifier is the customer information file number, the bank's internal ID for each customer.
The bank has not said whether the 3,897 records belong to 3,897 different people, or what the rest of the set contains. The 3,897 are roughly 1 in 100 of the records it examined.
Account numbers, balances, passwords, one-time passcodes, card details and government identity numbers such as PAN or Aadhaar are not among the categories the filing lists. The risk in the listed categories is impersonation: a caller or message that uses a customer's name, mobile number, date of birth, address, branch, and internal ID to appear to come from the bank.

articles.summary:
Plus de huit heures après les premières coupures ce mercredi 21 octobre, la panne mobile d’Orange et de Sosh se prolonge. L’opérateur confirme un incident national perturbant les appels, les SMS et les données mobiles d’une partie de ses clients. Le rétablissement complet des services reste attendu.
Le réseau revient chez certains abonnés, tandis que d’autres restent privés de service. Depuis les premières coupures signalées en fin de matinée, Orange a précisé l’ampleur des perturbations. Le constat dépasse désormais les seuls témoignages : l’opérateur reconnaît un incident national, sans avoir encore expliqué publiquement son origine.
Mise à jour du 21/10 à 19h30 : selon les informations de Numerama, la panne pourrait provenir d’une migration ratée d’une partie des abonnés vers un cœur de réseau 5G. La remise en cohérence des profils des lignes concernées compliquerait le rétablissement des services. Orange n’a pas confirmé cette explication dans sa réponse au média.
De son côté, RTL évoquait dans son dernier point qu'un retour à la normale serait envisagé autour de 21 heures, sous réserve de l’évolution de la panne. Cet horaire reste évidemment une estimation et aucun engagement officiel de l’opérateur n'a été communiqué. 
De nombreux lecteurs et lectrices nous ont fait savoir que le réseau était revenu pour eux, chez Sosh comme chez Orange. Ces premiers constats ne permettent toutefois pas encore de confirmer un rétablissement complet pour l'ensemble des clients.

articles.title: U.S. Orders DeepSeek Removed From Federal Civilian Systems, Bans New Purchases
articles.summary:
U.S. federal civilian agencies must remove DeepSeek products from their information technology systems, along with any third-party products or services "developed using DeepSeek implementations," under a Department of Homeland Security order.
They may also no longer buy information technology products or services from the Chinese AI developer or its affiliates
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin issued the order, dated July 24, 2026, under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018, and the department published it in the Federal Register on October 20. The notice does not define "DeepSeek implementations."
The order names Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd., the developer of the R1 and V3 models, and covers its affiliates as defined in federal acquisition rules. The company's privacy policy says it collects, processes and stores users' personal data in the People's Republic of China.
Under the 2018 law, the Federal Acquisition Security Council recommends exclusion and removal orders, and three officials may issue them: the Secretary of Homeland Security for civilian agencies, the Secretary of Defense for the Defense Department and national security systems, and the Director of National Intelligence for the intelligence community.
The DeepSeek order therefore covers only what civilian agencies buy and run. It does not restrict companies or the public.

articles.title: OpenAI quiere probar implantes cerebrales que puedan detectar y tratar el cáncer
articles.summary:
El fondo de inversión de OpenAI, conocido como OpenAI Startup Fund y Founders Fund de Peter Thiel, invirtieron en Coherence Neuro, una startup que desarrolla un implante cerebral capaz de detectar tumores y tratarlos con pulsos eléctricos. La compañía recaudó 45 millones de dólares en una ronda semilla.
Coherence entrena modelos de inteligencia artificial para interpretar las señales eléctricas que emiten los tumores cerebrales. Según la empresa, ya logró identificar esas señales en animales para determinar si un cáncer crece, se reduce o reaparece, y ahora busca trasladar esos hallazgos a pacientes humanos.
El dispositivo, del tamaño de una moneda, ya fue probado este año en tres personas que se sometían a una cirugía para extirpar tumores cerebrales en el Royal Melbourne Hospital, en Australia. El implante permaneció colocado unos 30 minutos antes de ser retirado, como primera prueba de seguridad.
La compañía avanza ahora con un segundo grupo de siete pacientes, en los que evaluará tanto la capacidad de registrar señales como la de aplicar estimulación eléctrica. El dispositivo también está diseñado para emitir pulsos eléctricos leves que frenen el crecimiento de los tumores a medida que los detecta.
Una vez que el implante quede colocado de forma permanente, una aplicación conectada permitirá a los pacientes registrar sus síntomas, que los médicos podrán usar para ajustar la estimulación eléctrica de forma remota o dejar que el propio dispositivo lo haga de manera automáti…

articles.title: SpaceX ya no vive solo de cohetes y satélites: la inteligencia artificial impulsa sus ingresos

SpaceX ya no depende solamente de los cohetes, los lanzamientos espaciales y Starlink, su servicio de internet satelital. El cambio en la composición del negocio responde a la expansión de Super Intelligence, la división que concentra los servicios de inteligencia artificial de SpaceX. La unidad generó USD 7.600 millones en ingresos, un crecimiento interanual cercano al 830%, y representó más de la mitad de la facturación total del trimestre.
El segmento combina actividades diferentes. Por un lado, ofrece infraestructura de computación en la nube, que permite a otras empresas utilizar capacidad informática para desarrollar y ejecutar sistemas de inteligencia artificial sin tener que construir toda esa infraestructura por su cuenta. articles.title: Attackers Abuse UpdraftCentral Keys to Plant Backdoors on WordPress Sites
articles.summary:
Unknown threat actors breached TeamUpdraft's website and potentially gained unauthorized access to customers' connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault, and UpdraftClone, using them to backdoor WordPress sites.
TeamUpdraft is the developer behind UpdraftPlus, a popular WordPress backup plugin with over four million active installations. The vendor also offers UpdraftCentral, a remote management service that's used for managing multiple sites remotely. A client component of UpdraftCentral is shipped within every copy of UpdraftPlus.
"Over the weekend of 17-18 October we identified unauthorized access to the teamupdraft.com website," TeamUpdraft said in a statement. "Our team responded straight away and worked through the night to contain it – we closed the access route, signed out every account and replaced the keys and credentials that could have been affected."
As a result of the incident, threat actors are believed to have accessed its customer database, which holds the following information -
- Names, email addresses, billing addresses and order history
- Account passwords, stored only in hashed (scrambled) form and never in plain text
- Two-factor authentication (2FA) settings
- Connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault and UpdraftClone
TeamUpdraft said the database does not hold any financial information, and that they are handled by Stripe and PayPal. It also emphasized that the UpdraftPlus plugin, along with self-hosted versions of UpdraftCentral and back…

articles.title: PHP2Shell: Two Unpatched Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVSS 9.2) Trigger Emergency Security Alert
articles.summary:
This story is developing and was written before PHP's scheduled 14:00 UTC release on October 21. Once the release is out, the affected and fixed versions below are confirmed by the official advisory.
PHP will ship an out-of-cycle security release at 14:00 UTC today, October 21, for two critical vulnerabilities that its security team has rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale but has not described.
Security researchers at watchTowr say the two flaws allow remote code execution. Only the four supported PHP branches, 8.2 through 8.5, can receive the fix, and no exploitation has been reported so far.
The advance notice followed a leak. On October 20, a post on HN said two PHP remote code execution flaws, rated CVSS 10.0 and affecting versions from PHP 5 onward, would be disclosed on Thursday, October 22. The poster said they had "no evidence beyond 'source: trust me, bro'".
watchTowr then posted on X that the leaked information was real, that the two flaws were under embargo, that everyone had been supposed to wait until Thursday, and that it could not share more for now.
PHP published its notice that evening, at 19:33 UTC, with the release set for Wednesday, a day before the date watchTowr gave. The notice says PHP may release earlier "should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild."
The leak carried the flaws' existence, a score, a date, and two CVE identifiers, not how the flaws work. The CVSS 10.0 figure is the lea…

articles.title: Attackers Hijacked Over 300 Tor Exit Relays to Intercept SSH Connections
articles.summary:
Attackers took control of more than 300 Tor exit relays in early October and used them to redirect SSH connections to servers that stole login passwords, a researcher found.
Exit relays are the last hop in a Tor circuit, where traffic leaves the network for its destination. Only a password login to an SSH server made through Tor between October 1 and 5, after accepting the interception server's host key, could have been captured.
The Tor Project began flagging relays on October 4, and by October 5, none remained in the consensus, the list of relays that Tor clients use. At the peak on October 4, the relays carrying the attacker's exit policy made up 7.46% of Tor's exit capacity, measured by consensus weight, according to an analysis of public Tor directory data posted to the tor-relays mailing list.
The researcher, who publishes as kaba, scanned all of Tor's roughly 3,000 exits on October 2 and found 333 redirecting SSH to the same 12 interception servers. The directory-data analysis counts 377 relays run by 59 operators that switched to the attacker's exit policy between October 1 and 4, which it calls "a policy match, not proof of compromise."
How the Hijacked Exits Intercepted SSH
An exit relay only carries traffic to the ports its exit policy allows. The attackers rewrote that policy in the relays' torrc configuration files to allow port 22 (the SSH port), enabling SSH on 342 relays that had blocked it. Another 24 relays that had not been exits at all became exits.

articles.title: The Harness Is the Hard Part of Agentic Pentesting
articles.summary:
An AppSec team can point an AI agent running on a general-purpose model at its own web apps with little setup. Sure, the model writes the attacks. But everything that makes those attacks safe to run against production and worth acting on afterward lives in the harness around the model. The harness is where the engineering in AI pentesting sits. The Hugging Face intrusion OpenAI disclosed in July showed what happens when that harness gives way, even inside an OpenAI evaluation built to contain the agents.
Why Each Control Takes Rigorous Engineering
Let’s take a closer look at the attack different stages and the role AI agents can take there
Scope
A pentesting agent makes thousands of decisions about where to send its next request, and the model judges each one against a rule written in plain language. A web app’s real boundary often extends past one domain through redirects and calls to outside services. Enforcing scope means code that inspects every request before it leaves, and OWASP’s 2026 guidance routes privileged actions through a deterministic policy engine that checks them at execution time, outside the model.
Credentials
Finding exposed credentials is part of what a pentest does, so the agent regularly comes across working keys outside its assignment. Which of those it may use, for what, and when a person gets involved are policy decisions that the code around the model applies on every attempt.

articles.title: Generative AI Is Erasing Behavioral Tells, Weakening Behavior-Only Detection, Proofpoint Reports
articles.summary:
Generative AI has changed what a malicious email looks like. Messages that once gave themselves away through clumsy wording, generic pretexts, and reused templates now arrive fluent, personalized, and unique to each recipient, and the behavioral signals email filters have relied on for years are fading as a result.
Proofpoint shared several examples of the shift at its Protect 2026 conference. In one, a single threat actor contacted more than 30 real estate agents at the same company, each from a different account, about a different property, and in different words, before closing every thread with the same request: join a video meeting.
Federal data points the same way. The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center counted more than 22,000 complaints involving AI in 2025, with nearly $900 million in associated losses, and logged 24,768 business email compromise (BEC) complaints with about $3.05 billion in reported losses, according to its 2025 Internet Crime Report.
What AI Changed
Email filters were built for attackers who had to cut corners. Researching a target, writing convincingly in a second language, impersonating a supplier, and producing enough variants to defeat signatures all took time, so attackers reused templates and infrastructure, and that reuse left patterns. Behavioral detection learned to spot them: new infrastructure, awkward language, odd timing, and requests that did not fit the conversation.

articles.summary:
PHP has released emergency updates that fix two critical flaws in the language itself, letting an attacker without an account run code on a web server. The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the PHP team says only updating fully protects a server.
The flaws, together called PHP2Shell, sit in the PHP runtime, not in any application, so a site is exposed even when its own code is secure. The risk is highest on servers using Apache's mod_php, where a working exploit triggers the attack before any application code runs.
Both flaws are rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale and carry the identifiers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. PHP published them around the scheduled release time of 14:00 UTC on October 21, a day after details leaked ahead of a planned October 22 disclosure.
Researchers at Wiz, Calif, and OpenAI found and reported the flaws, which affect nearly every PHP version back to PHP 5.4.
Who Is Affected
Every PHP installation that serves web requests is at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed, according to the PHP security advisory.
Because the flaws are in the engine rather than in any site's code, even a simple "Hello World" page on a vulnerable PHP version can be attacked.

The popular LiteLLM Python package has been compromised as part of a software supply chain attack that delivered a credential stealer and a backdoor, according to reports from SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity, and Upwind.
The compromise affects LiteLLM 1.107.0, distributed through PyPI wheels and Docker images. The Python package has since been quarantined on Python Package Index (PyPI), and the malicious Docker images have been removed.
Oliver Jensen, director of security at LiteLLM, said an investigation into the incident is ongoing, and that it's still working to trace the original attack vector by which the threat actor published the malicious release.
"We have identified that the malicious actions were taken through three engineers' GitHub accounts, appearing to be by way of stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens," Jensen said. "The threat actor used one user's account to trigger the project-releaser run, and another user's account to approve it. All tokens which were involved in this attack have been revoked."
"We have not yet identified the mechanism by which the threat actor acquired the relevant tokens, so cannot yet assert that no further access to these GitHub accounts. As a temporary mitigation, we have removed all but one (unaffected) user from our GitHub organization."
Separately, LiteLLM said it has updated the public registries to remove any trusted links to its GitHub organization so as to prevent further publication of malicious packages.

articles.title: Meta acumula más de USD 50 mil millones en sanciones económicas en los últimos 7 años: estos son los casos
articles.summary:
El camino regulatorio y judicial de Meta se convirtió en los últimos años en una constante batalla legal, marcada por un cambio radical en la severidad de las sanciones económicas globales: la más reciente de ellas, una multa de 25.000 millones de dólares en EE. UU.
Lo que comenzó como un severo castigo por malas prácticas de privacidad escaló en los años siguientes hacia una ofensiva internacional centrada en la protección de datos transfronterizos y, de manera más reciente, en el impacto psicológico y la seguridad de los menores de edad. Así, en solo siete años, la compañía de Mark Zuckerberg ya ha acumulado alrededor de 52.261 millones de dólares en multas y acuerdos financieros.
El caso Cambridge Analytica con Facebook
El año 2019 marcó el primer gran punto de inflexión. Tras meses de escrutinio, la Comisión Federal de Comercio de los Estados Unidos (FTC) impuso una sanción histórica de 5.000 millones de dólares a Facebook. El motivo fue el uso indebido y la filtración de datos de más de 87 millones de usuarios a la consultora política Cambridge Analytica.
Esta multa no solo representó una cifra récord en el sector tecnológico, sino que estableció el precedente de que las grandes corporaciones de Silicon Valley tendrían que rendir cuentas financieramente a gran escala por sus brechas de privacidad.

articles.title: Panne Orange et Sosh : l'opérateur officialise LA bonne nouvelle de la journée, et en dit plus sur l'incident
articles.summary:
Le réseau mobile Orange est rétabli après près de dix heures de panne. Dans un communiqué diffusé mercredi soir, l’opérateur attribue l’incident à la défaillance d’un équipement de son cœur de réseau, sans en dire davantage.
La panne Orange et Sosh qui a privé le réseau mobile de signal depuis la fin de matinée ce mercredi 21 octobre est terminée, du moins selon l'opérateur. Dans un communiqué diffusé peu après 21 h, Orange assure que les appels, les SMS et les usages mobiles fonctionnent de nouveau, et évoque « une défaillance d'un équipement au niveau de notre cœur de réseau mobile ». Une explication qui rejoint en partie celle du hacker éthique SaxX, lequel parlait d'une migration vers un nouveau cœur de réseau 5G, une piste précise que l'opérateur ne reprend pas à son compte.
Un équipement du cœur de réseau à l'origine de la panne Orange
Il aura donc fallu attendre la fin de la crise pour obtenir une explication officielle, même sommaire. Mercredi, un équipement du cœur de réseau mobile d'Orange a flanché. Plus tôt dans l'après-midi, Clément Domingo, aka SaxX, avait publié des « infos exclusives » glanées selon lui en interne. « Ce n'est pas un hack », assurait-il avec ce brin de piquant qu'on lui connaît, avant d'expliquer qu'Orange introduisait un nouveau cœur de réseau mobile 5G, sur lequel les lignes migrées étaient « a priori » hors service. Il évoquait aussi des centaines de milliers de particuliers et d'entreprises touchés. Dans son communiqué, l'opérateur ne parle…

articles.title: Airbnb prohibió que los anfitriones obliguen a los huéspedes a hacer tareas de limpieza
articles.summary:
Airbnb prohibió a los anfitriones incluir en sus reglas de la casa tareas que exijan un esfuerzo significativo o que normalmente realizaría una persona de limpieza, como lavar los platos, sacar la basura o quitar las sábanas de la cama. La nueva política regirá para las reservas hechas a partir del 20 de noviembre.
Según el detalle publicado por la empresa, los anfitriones podrán pedirles a los huéspedes que dejen los platos usados en la pileta, pero no que los laven y los guarden. También podrán solicitar que junten las toallas usadas, pero no que quiten las sábanas ni que pongan a lavar la ropa de cama.
Respecto de la basura, los anfitriones solo pueden pedir que se separen los residuos en los contenedores internos de la vivienda, no que se los saque del lugar. La misma lógica se aplica a servicios como el aire acondicionado: pueden pedir que se apague al irse, pero no que el huésped evite usar una comodidad incluida en el anuncio.
“Hemos escuchado de nuestra comunidad que (las reglas de la casa) pueden ser confusas, engorrosas y difíciles de manejar”, dijo Airbnb en un comunicado difundido a Euronews Travel. “Por eso las rediseñamos para que sean más fáciles de encontrar y más claras de establecer, junto con una nueva política que mantiene los pedidos razonables, sin sorpresas”.

articles.title: Brouillés en vain, des drones ont survolé de nuit la base navale de Toulon
articles.summary:
Les militaires étaient en plein exercice de protection de la rade de Toulon quand de « gros engins » ont survolé de nuit la base navale et deux autres sites de l’armée. Malgré le brouillage, aucun n’a été récupéré, et les enquêteurs cherchent encore qui les pilotait.
Pendant l’exercice interarmées Typhon, organisé du 5 au 16 octobre, l’armée a entraîné ses forces à défendre le port militaire de Toulon, avec des manœuvres aériennes où des drones étaient engagés. D’autres drones, non autorisés ceux-là, ont survolé de nuit la base navale, un site de la Direction générale de l’armement (DGA) et le 54e régiment d’artillerie d’Hyères entre le 9 et le 13 octobre, selon ICI Provence. « Ils étaient en tout cas plusieurs à chaque fois, et des gros engins », a confié une source à nos confrères. La préfecture maritime a confirmé ces survols, et le parquet de Toulon a ouvert une enquête judiciaire. Même avec des équipes en alerte pour l’exercice, la Marine ne sait toujours pas combien d’engins ont survolé ses sites, ni à qui ils appartenaient.
Aucun drone récupéré malgré le brouillage
« À ce jour, aucune infrastructure sensible n’a été menacée », assure la Marine. À chaque survol, ses équipes ont réagi. « Pour chaque occurrence, les mesures de sécurité prévues ont été activées par le déclenchement de dispositifs anti-drone, coordonnées avec les forces de sécurité intérieures », indique le communiqué du commandement de zone Méditerranée.
